it is estimated that in the european union today, approximately 1% of the total amount of medicines that reach patients legally through the pharmacy network are counterfeit. this percentage is constantly increasing. it's about people's health. counterfeit medicines may have different effects from the pills prescribed by your doctor. they can be life-threatening. counterfeiting is a crime and must be subject to specific sanctions. the new legislation i support brings more security features as well as sanctions for counterfeiters. it defines a control system to improve the identification of medicines so that in the future the flows of medicines can be traced from the manufacturer to the consumer. the new rules also cover the sale of medicines via the internet. it is one of the most widely used means of bringing counterfeit products to the european union markets.

if we are forced today to vote on a report on the protection of patients from falsified medicines, it is partly because the market liberalism advocated by the european commission has opened the door to the market for falsified products. unregulated competition leads to the falsification of medicines for the benefit of companies. the consumer is the victim. i voted for this report even though i am not entirely convinced that the definition of counterfeit is the right one. in addition, it is not entirely clear who should be punished when a counterfeit medicine is found. but this is a first step in the right direction and we shall see in a year's time whether our action has been effective.
we're breaking the standard that says fake drugs. we know that after weapons, drugs, the pharmaceutical industry makes the biggest profits, and it's no coincidence that criminals are focused on falsifying medicines to mislead our fellow citizens, our patients. how often a drug that is supposed to treat cancer or heart disease contains no active ingredient at all or only a small percentage, and this is actually a crime that endangers the health, and how often the life, of the patient. it is good that we have adopted principles in this text, new principles that tighten the punishment of those who commit criminal activity in this area, and i am glad that europe has taken a step in the right direction. of course, selling on the internet, but also selling through the normal, classic delivery system, which often sells counterfeit medicines, will be better controlled.

for the efd group. compared to traditional gas sources, extraction from non-traditional sources today represents only about 5% of the world's total gas production. non-traditional sources have a lower concentration of raw material than traditional sources. in addition to coal methane or gas hidden in low-permeability rocks or gas hydrates, shale gas appears to be the most promising source. the best experience with its extraction is in north america, where extraction from non-traditional sources accounted for up to 42% of total production in 2007. the international energy agency estimates that europe could also have up to 991 billion cubic metres of unconventional gas reserves. they should be located in particular in poland, germany, hungary, romania, sweden and the united kingdom. between 2007 and 2010, poland issued almost 60 licenses for shale gas exploration and production. the licences are also held by major global energy companies. it is therefore clear from the above that these new non-traditional gas sources are also becoming an attractive alternative for the use of new horizontal extraction technologies.

looking at the history of european integration and the current organisation and functioning of the european union, it can be seen that the european union can be seen not only as a grouping of states but increasingly as a political arena with the potential to create a genuine european public. the union has not only a single market, its own legislation, an elected representative body or its own judiciary. political parties at european level have also been a reality for some time. they are not just a gathering of national parties. they have their own agenda, a european agenda, and are an integral part of the european political public. strengthening political parties at european level will consolidate participatory governance in the european union and, ultimately, democracy. for these reasons, i welcome the proposal presented for reform of the statute and funding of political parties at union level and i would like to thank you, mr vice-president, personally for your cooperation. it is now very important for political parties to have a common and uniform legal status. the difference between the political party regime and the rules applicable to the european institutions needs to be overcome. this is possible through the introduction of a common political, legal and fiscal status for political parties at european level. it would also be appropriate to consider that only political parties operating at national or regional level should have the right to establish such a party. there is also the question of the financing system. the system for approving the finances of political parties at european level should be simplified. in order to maintain transparency, it should be possible to carry out financial controls. a transparent and secure environment for the operation and funding of european political parties is a desirable and welcome step towards citizens of the member states of the european union. it can help them in their daily lives. the status of political parties at european level is a significant step towards greater interaction with citizens, an increase in the level of democracy and an increase in public interest in european issues.
the report on the application of the regulation on the statute and the financing of political parties at european level shall assess the experience gained in applying this legal standard to the governance of political entities with a broad european scope. in addition to assessing the current situation, ms giannakou also decided to make a number of proposals to improve the current legal environment. perhaps the most significant change should be the change of the statute form from the current belgian equivalent of an ngo to a common and uniform european legal statute for political parties. the second major change should be to adjust the percentage of independent funding sources to 10% of the total budget for political parties. however, given that in 2012 european political parties and their foundations are expected to receive more than eur 30 million from the european parliament, it will be necessary to ensure maximum transparency in the management of those funds. such changes can be encouraged to further improve political work in the european union.
in writing i do not want to be a member of a european political party that will be founded on the principles outlined in the report submitted. these parties are supposed to represent the 'european public interest', but if you ask any two members of this parliament what that is like, they will each say something different. who determines this interest? the parliament? the commission? but meps are not nominated by the eu institutions, they are elected by citizens in the member states. my duty is to represent individual citizens, not what the eu institutions consider to be the 'european public interest'. i also do not agree that the european parties should also act at regional and national level. they just don't have a mandate to do that. if they do, they will come into conflict with the parties on whose ticket we were all elected and with the voters those parties represent. and my loyalty is to my constituents, not to a european political party. it's called a free mandate. so i strongly disagree with the philosophy of the super-site presented in this report. it's another attempt by euro-social engineers who are so obsessed with the utopia of the superstate that they ignore common sense. if they had listened to him, they would have known that by stubbornly pushing such proposals, they are undermining the foundations on which european integration rests. as a committed european, i must therefore vote against this report.
the drive to create a single market for businesses and growth is confronted with many administrative obstacles, which are a natural consequence of the fact that the business environment in the member states has developed separately at different stages and under different conditions. the effort to synchronise the business environment of all 27 member states seems to me to be a very challenging ambition. i would therefore also like to draw attention to the possibility of an alternative procedure which does not require the absolute cooperation of all member states from the outset. the procedure under article 20 of the treaty on european union, the so-called enhanced cooperation in the area of the creation of unitary patent protection, has already succeeded in bringing the long-standing problem of the european patent significantly forward. i am convinced that if the will of a group of member states, particularly those with stronger economies such as france and germany, could be found to unify accounting rules and to establish a common accounting and tax system, it would be possible, through enhanced cooperation under article 20 of the treaty on european union, to lay the foundations of a common accounting system to which other member states could gradually join. i am convinced that a good selection of well-thought-out steps can make a significant contribution to the functioning of the european union's single market.
it is often the case that the preservation of the single market comes at the expense of social rights and the observance of certain national traditions in the labour market. in addition, the single market is currently facing other problems, as the economic crisis is negatively impacting the prospects for its further successful development. however, i believe that it is necessary to include a social component in legislation relating to the single market in order to ensure that the policy in question is genuinely targeted at citizens and that coherence is ensured, also by respecting social and workers' rights. it should be a common endeavour to make the single market and its functioning a benefit for citizens and businesses alike, and thus contribute to an overall increase in european competitiveness. legislative measures must also be geared to achieving objectives such as a stable and responsible remuneration policy and adequate representation of women in senior management positions.
the idea that europeans should create more jobs, more job opportunities is fundamental to us. in particular, it must be borne in mind that the citizen must be at the very heart of the initiative, whether from the point of view of consumer rights, communication strategies or copyright, improving the environment for cross-border operations of smes, which are the backbone of every economy. the process of recognition of professional qualifications needs to be accelerated in order to increase mobility as well as reflection in collective agreements. i also consider it crucial to implement the same legislation in all member states, to ensure adequate social protection, and i repeat, social protection, and to combat social exclusion. finally, mr president, i would like to say that the incorporation of these elements into the european qualifications framework will ensure real benefits for citizens as well as an efficient labour mobility mechanism.
in writing. the single market is vital for the future growth of the union's economy. special attention should be paid to small and medium-sized enterprises, as they have the greatest potential for growth and job creation. the single market should benefit small businesses, which provide the majority of jobs but have greater difficulty in exploiting the opportunities offered by the single market. they have a problem with funding development, with funding innovation. equal attention should be paid to local businesses in disadvantaged, sparsely populated areas and in urban areas facing difficulties. competition policy is a key tool in enabling the eu to have a dynamic, efficient and innovative internal market and to be competitive on the world stage. the eu needs to take important measures to improve access to information for smes, to make them aware of the opportunities offered by the single market and the financial instruments provided by the union. i personally consider it important to integrate the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and the elements of the small business package into all eu policies relating to the single market. this is key to overcoming the current obstacles at national and european level.
strengthening democracy in the european union requires a continuous effort to enhance a fair and transparent environment for the functioning and funding of political parties at european level. union citizens should be more involved in political life at eu level and it is therefore necessary to create favourable incentive conditions for the activities of political parties. for example, to prevent less than 20% of eligible voters from voting in the european parliament elections, as happened in my country. i agree with the idea that such political parties should have a common and uniform legal status, as well as their own legal personality, which is directly derived from the rules of the european union treaties. as regards the funding system, transparency is intrinsically linked to the application of values and therefore clear funding conditions must be a first priority.
the volume of the internal market in goods in the european union represents 17% of the world market in goods. the volume of internal trade in services in the european union represents 28% of world trade in services. if this mass is set in motion in the right direction, the results in the form of economic growth based on the dynamics of own resources should be achieved. however, this is only possible if the proposed measures, which i have supported, are implemented in such a way as to eliminate bottlenecks in the movement of people, capital, goods and services between the various countries of the union, and to increase the availability and reliability of credit and banking services, as well as of online transactions. this is only the case if a more functional single market opens up new potential for the realisation of european union-originated products and activities on european union markets. then a 4% contribution to economic growth over ten years might not be a utopia.

on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, commissioner, i really appreciate the commission’s strong commitment to condemning violence against women as a weapon of war – used systematically in armed conflict for a variety of purposes including humiliation, intimidation, political terror, extracting information, rewarding soldiers, and even ethnic cleansing. violence against women in armed conflict is largely based on traditional views of women as property. because women in many cultures play the role of transmitters of culture and symbols of nations, violence against women is also used as a means of attacking a society’s values and its honour. the rome statute of the international criminal court recognises sexual violence as part of an attack against civilians – against humanity – as being a war crime. various forms of sexual violence in armed conflict, including sexual slavery, forced marriage and forced pregnancy, are war crimes and should be considered as grave breaches of the geneva convention. too often, those responsible for acts of sexual violence in war go unpunished; too often, violence against women is accepted as an unavoidable part of war; too often, its perpetrators are granted amnesty as part of peace deals. it is time to condemn these inhuman practices in any part of the world, and our message today should be that perpetrators of these war crimes can no longer go unpunished.
sexual violence is not a violation of women's or men's human rights. there's no such thing. it is a crime against human dignity, which is one of the fundamental rights of every human being, woman and man. this applies not only to europe but also to egypt, libya, the congo and the other countries of africa and the middle east referred to in this resolution. military conflicts must not be an extenuating circumstance. in the congo, it started with the rape of women, and now men are being raped. but resolutions are just words. we need to act. the commission must start to monitor human rights violations in the world in detail and, at the same time, must devise the instruments by which europe will, if necessary, enforce them. otherwise, the partnerships we're investing so much in might as well be called pay-as-you-go.

for the s&d group. good evening, madam president, commissioner, colleagues, colleagues. i have been informed that the commission has decided to withdraw the proposal. in the age of a globalised economy, the european union's common trade policy seems to us to be something quite natural. the initiative to coordinate investment policy at european union level is therefore equally normal. the current system based on a number of overlapping and sometimes conflicting bilateral investment agreements between member states should be replaced within a reasonable timeframe by a new framework of investment agreements of the european union. these should be in line with the horizontal objectives of the union's policies and i would personally like to advocate that the main emphasis be placed on development policy in particular. i agree with the rapporteur that the transition to a new regime should not happen overnight. it should take place within a pre-planned transitional period, the length and rules of which should be known in advance in order to avoid legal uncertainty. without such a timetable, the regulation would allow for the creation of parallel, potentially incompatible investment schemes. a sufficiently long transitional period is necessary to make the dual open-ended system unacceptable to parliament in this union investment policy. investment policy is a full competence of the european union under the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
madam president, commissioner, the issue of protecting crossborder investment in the countries of the european union has become extremely complex and sensitive since the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. more than 1200 bilateral investment agreements concluded by member states under different legal regimes, in many cases incompatible, need to be comprehensively transferred under the aegis of the european union while preserving the rights of the parties involved. the principle of the coexistence of agreements during a transitional period, which would allow member states to renegotiate the existence of a bilateral agreement or, in accordance with the investment policy of the european union, to complete the negotiations on those agreements which have been worked out, is perhaps the only possible way out of the legal morass created by the transfer of competence from the member states to the european union. however, it will be important to maintain the proper cooperation of the commission with the member states throughout this process, so that there is no real loss of legal certainty for investors and counterparties.

in 1990, józsef antall declared himself prime minister of all hungarians, including hungarians living outside the territory of hungary. today, viktor orbán is going further. a new constitution was adopted in which hungary proclaims the idea of a single hungarian nation, comprised of all hungarians, understood as persons of hungarian nationality regardless of their citizenship. this constitution also provides that hungary bears responsibility for the fate of hungarians abroad. that provision is contrary to international law, which holds that the state in which a national minority is situated is responsible for the promotion and protection of that minority. the new hungarian constitution also supports efforts to create collective self-governments of hungarian minorities living abroad on an ethnic basis. the provisions of the hungarian constitution can be a means of interfering in the internal affairs of foreign states, thus creating a seed of tension between hungary and the neighbouring countries. this is contrary to the spirit of democratic europe.

current studies of the impacts of climate change on forests in europe indicate a wide range of specific regional responses of forest ecosystems. the ability to cope with the nature and scale of the expected problems depends on the natural conditions of the region for example, mountain areas are exposed to different problems than lowland areas , on the physiological sensitivity of forest vegetation and the ready adaptation potential of individual ecosystems, on the expected intensity of climate change for central and eastern europe, for example, projected change one and a half times stronger than the global average, and on the technical capabilities of the forestry sector to implement adaptation measures, for example by changing the timber composition in favour of resistant species. it is therefore essential to take into account local and regional specificities, while respecting the specific characteristics of protected habitats, when designing protection and adaptation measures.
i was interested to hear about the problems of communicating with the european council on the implementation of its chapter on the general budget. as far as i know, one of the basic requirements of a parliamentary mandate is to control the executive branch. the council, the commission and the other institutions of the european union administer the funds of the citizens of the european union in accordance with agreed rules. it is therefore natural that the elected representatives of the people, on behalf of the taxpayers, check the institutions to see that they are handling the citizens' money carefully and in accordance with the agreed rules. it works the same way in all democratic countries. i therefore do not understand the european council's refusal to give us the necessary cooperation in assessing its budget. we are not asking whether mr sarkozy or mrs merkel go to a better or a worse restaurant or whether they buy a better or a worse bag or whether they dress at one company or another, we are asking how they spend the public money of the taxpayers, and we have the full right to do so and they have the full obligation to provide this information.

in writing. − units of measurement are essential in the use of all measuring instruments to express measurements or any indication of quantity. they are used in almost all fields of human activity and it is therefore necessary to ensure the greatest possible clarity in their use and set rules for their use within the european union for economic, public health, public safety or administrative purposes. member states should be able to require that measuring devices on their territory bear indications of quantity in a single legal unit of measurement. this directive supports the smooth functioning of the internal market through the degree of harmonisation of units of measurement. in this context it is appropriate for the commission to monitor market developments relating to this directive and its implementation, particularly with regard to possible barriers to the internal market and further harmonisation needed to overcome these obstacles.

in writing. − the treaty aims to maintain an economic union with healthy competition and properties that are similar to those on the domestic market. as regards manufactured tobacco, the achievement of this aim presupposes that the application in the member states of taxes affecting the consumption of products in this sector does not distort conditions of competition and does not impede their free movement within the european union. as far as excise duties are concerned, the harmonisation of structures must, in particular, result in competition in the different categories of manufactured tobacco belonging to the same group not being distorted by the effects of charging the tax and, consequently, in the opening of the member states’ national markets. the imperative needs of competition imply a system of freely formed prices for all groups of manufactured tobacco and implementation of this policy needs to guarantee a high level of human health.
in writing. − the european single coinage system should inspire public confidence and include technological innovations to ensure that it is secure, reliable and effective. public confidence in the system depends on the physical properties of coins, which should be as user-friendly as possible. after consultations with consumer associations, european blind union representatives and the vending machines industry, research was carried out to take into account the specific requirements of important categories of coin users. in order to ensure a smooth changeover to the euro and to facilitate acceptance of the coinage systems by users, easy distinction between coins through visual and tactile characteristics needed to be guaranteed. the coins need to be covered with some special security features to limit the scope for fraud. the fact that they have one european and one national side is an appropriate expression of the idea of european monetary union between the member states.
in writing. − the current absence of harmonised rules on origin marking puts the eu at a disadvantage and also deprives european producers of origin-sensitive consumer goods of the opportunity to reap the benefits associated with producing within the union, while consumers miss the opportunity to have access to information on the origin of products. origin marking would facilitate consumer choice and contribute to reducing fraudulent, inaccurate or misleading claims of origin. this amendment introduces a requirement to indicate the presence of non-textile parts of animal origin in textile products. it should be highlighted that fur is often used as trimming in relatively inexpensive garments, which are often imported from asia. in order to eliminate potential obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market caused by diverging provisions or practices by member states, and in order to keep pace with the development of electronic commerce and future challenges in the market for textile products, it is necessary to examine the harmonisation and standardisation of other aspects of textile labelling with a view to facilitating the free movement of textile products in the internal market and achieving a uniform and high level of consumer protection throughout the eu.
in writing. − in council regulation (ec) 2007/2000, the european union granted exceptional unlimited duty-free access to eu markets for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the main objective of these measures is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. in addition, economic development has promoted political stability throughout the region. these trade preferences were granted for the period that ended on 31 december 2010 and currently apply to bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo. the abolition of trade preferences could, however, have very negative consequences on the overall economic performance of the western balkans and consequently a negative effect on their domestic reforms and the transformation process. moreover, it could seriously jeopardize the economic recovery. in order not to disrupt trade, it is therefore desirable to extend the application of council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 to 31 december 2015.
in writing. − the european union is the world's biggest economy. the need for one single internal market is crucial for europe to take leadership in the global economy, with a focus on the service sector and the knowledge economy. the digital agenda and the digital economy can serve as a spearhead for making the internal market a reality for all parts of our economy. this requires an ability to take the lead on broadband and use of the internet. it is crucial for the european telecom industry to regain global leadership, but also in order to take the lead in the development of information technologies as such and in the emergence of new services and applications. even more importantly, it is also crucial in order to create a momentum for higher productivity, cohesion, competitiveness, and access to one single market for the european industry as a whole. we must aim to make europe the best and make what is best for europe: opening up new services and increased mobile traffic, laying the ground for new opportunities for culture and content, broadcasters and public services in the framework of broadband, and at the same time securing the same opportunities for broadcasting as of today.
in writing. - broadcasting frequencies are a national asset. european legislation must therefore respect the sovereignty of the member states in pursuing a common european interest in the use of these frequencies. on the other hand, the interests of slovakia and the other member states are in this area. the use of free bands for high-quality and fast data transmission benefits both citizens and businesses. european coordination is important here, as internet technologies are not limited by borders and their contribution grows with the number of participants. the aim of this proposal was to start addressing the issue of freed spectrum as soon as possible, so that europe could have a head start on other strong economies. this will create new jobs, new services and attract new investment to europe.
in writing. − following the ratification of the lisbon treaty, parliament’s powers have been strengthened and it is now co-legislator in almost all areas under the ordinary legislative procedure. as a result, it is the focus of attention of an even larger number of lobbyists, who, moreover, play a key role in the open, pluralist dialogue on which a democratic system is based, and act as an important source of information for members in the context of the performance of their duties. in the light of these developments, against this constitutional background and in keeping with their commitment to transparency, parliament and the commission have agreed to establish and maintain a joint register in order to keep a list of the names of, and exercise scrutiny over, the organisations and individuals who take part in the drafting and implementation of eu policies. one of the important corrective measures necessary is to improve the rules on lobbying firms’ reporting of expenditure incurred for lobbying activities. the current legislation allows lobbyists to report much less than is actually incurred. equally important is transparency with regard to the financial resources from which a lobbying and consulting company draws its revenue.
in writing. − transparency of political institutions is a prerequisite for legitimacy. it should be easy to scrutinise how decisions are made, what the influences are behind them and how resources, i.e. taxpayer’s money, are allocated. therefore rules for lobbying are ultimately a question of legitimacy. parliament was the first european institution to address the phenomenon of an increasing number of interest groups at european level, and in particular the consequences of this evolution for the legislative process. while registration is not obligatory, it can be considered as such ‘de facto’ because permanent access to parliament’s premises is granted only to registered representatives. however, it is desirable for the future to achieve a system of registration that is obligatory ‘de jure’. the common register ensures the widest participation of all categories of operators while respecting their different or specific identities. the new name ‘transparency register’ makes it easier for non-commercial organisations to join the register. this will be a step forward towards greater transparency in the european institutions, and i hope it will contribute to giving the european project greater legitimacy among europe’s citizens.
in writing. - lobbying is a legitimate activity. it's one of the basic manifestations of democracy. because representative democracy can only work when citizens communicate with their elected representatives and ask them to promote their interests. in this respect, it is irrelevant whether citizens turn to politicians as individuals, associations, or as trading companies or manufacturing enterprises. no regulation may therefore restrict one of the fundamental rights of citizens. but the reasons why an elected representative chooses to put one interest above another must be motivated by conviction, not personal gain. and the transparency of a member's work in dealing with people who are promoting their interests is perhaps the best tool to prevent corruption in the making of laws. i therefore support the proposed common register, which takes account of the different nature of interest groups and distinguishes between those who lobby to increase their profit and those who approach elected representatives to achieve more good for society as a whole.
in writing. − financial risk is essential to the existence of the financial sector, and is equally essential in terms of both the business success of that sector and security functions for the economy in general. however, it is in the public interest that risks should be restricted to prevent systemic crisis. this challenge, as important as it is complex, can be met by means of a package of measures which will have either direct or indirect impact. financial institutions should be obliged to prepare annual reports on the adequacy and effectiveness of their internal control systems, and boards should have these reports adopted. financial institutions should give greater attention to the implementation of measures to raise awareness about the risks, as better information about risk at all levels of society – and among employees – is often crucial in improving risk management.
in writing. − forests and other wooded land account for more than 42% of eu territory, providing a livelihood to millions of workers and entrepreneurs and 16 million forest owners. forest sector industries provide more than 2 million jobs, and forestry employs 350 000 people. among the common policies with an impact on forest protection are environmental policy, energy, industry and trade policies, as well as policy coherence, including regional policy and the solidarity fund. given the scale of the threats and the total area of forests in the eu, the financing should increase, eligibility to receive assistance should be extended to public bodies and producer groups, and contributions should be paid on an area basis and should cover protective measures.
in writing. − the report was adopted in the committee on foreign affairs by an overwhelming majority. it has achieved a balanced approach to the most pressing issues concerning the organisation and activities of the european external action service (eeas) and to key issues for the common foreign and security policy (cfsp), such as promotion of the values of democracy, human rights and the rule of law, promotion of gender equality and energy security, the situation in iran and in afghanistan, the eu response to the democratic changes in the southern mediterranean region, and relations with major players such as russia, china, japan and india. the report strikes a balance on civilian-military cooperation in crisis resolution and on eu-nato interaction: on the one hand, it avoids relegating the eu exclusively to trade, development and humanitarian issues, the course pursued by the ecr group, and, on the other, it rejects the gue/ngl group’s insistence on excluding any military component from the cfsp.
in writing. − this report, which is in five parts – headed respectively security and foreign policy, security and defence, external and internal security, security through operations and security in partnership – provides a clear vision of how the eu should pursue its common security and defence policy in order to become an autonomous strategic player and to act as a force for security and stability in europe and the world.
in writing. − the eu is the largest contributor of development aid and the most important trade bloc but representation of the union, as such, in multilateral organisations remains fragmented. on the other hand, the eu member states are over-represented in all multilateral organisations with the exception of the world trade organization. this over-representation – particularly in the bretton woods institutions – often results in dissonance among the european voices and is perceived as hugely problematic by the emerging powers, which consider the status quo to be unfair. it would be appropriate that, in areas of exclusive competence, the eu should be the pre-eminent actor, with full membership, while the member states might also – but not necessarily – be present as members, without, in most cases, an independent role.
i don't want to look for a culprit, but i think the failure of the conciliation process is a failure, and we've poured dirty water on the baby. cloning is not only a complex but also a sensitive subject. dolly the sheep was neither the first nor the last animal to be cloned. tens of thousands more fail. deformed fetuses with oversized organs die in the wombs of the animals, others are stillborn, others die within days of birth. cloning is worse than animal abuse, like small cages or transport in a truck without water. therefore, the prohibition of the sale of cloned animals and their offspring is part of the novel food regulation. i don't think the complexity of the cloning issue is a priority right now. we should now send a clear signal to food producers that products from suffering animals do not belong on the european market.

portugal is another country that needs financial help from the euro, but let's be honest: we have to say that labelling this crisis as a 'debt' or a 'euro crisis' is very misleading. it gives the impression that the euro is in crisis because some member states are not managing their affairs in a rational way and are over-indebted. but ireland and portugal have managed with discipline and have been hit by a crisis they did not cause. the irresponsible were the poorly regulated banks. and it was the cost of bailing out these banks that got some of the eurozone countries into financial trouble. the current crisis is therefore more of a crisis of the european banking sector. if we are honest, the euro, or the new form of the euro, will certainly not be enough after 2013. the cost of saving the euro needs to be reduced by forcing commercial banks to admit losses, and the next step should be effective regulation of the financial sector.
innovation is one of the main drivers of europe's competitiveness, without which the strategic objectives set cannot be achieved. for example, the areas of public health and environmental protection are those most in need of innovation. the union and the member states must therefore provide financial or fiscal incentives to enterprises, individuals to focus scientific and technical research r&d in less lucrative but highly beneficial areas for the public. in my view, we are still allocating relatively small amounts of the budget to research, and i therefore stress the need for funding instruments in this area in future european union budgets. the european research area would also support the introduction of a single european patent, which, in addition to protecting the intellectual property of innovators, has the potential to reduce lengthy and costly bureaucratic processes and avoid repeated applications from a single entity in all member states.
for the efd group according to a report by the international labour organisation, domestic work accounts for about 5% of total employment. it is an invisible form of employment that takes place, not in a factory, a store, or an office, but in the homes of individuals. the workers are 90% women, who do not work in a collective, but alone within four walls. the aim of their work is not to produce added value but to provide care or services corresponding to the tasks that women normally perform in their own homes free of charge. as a result, this work is not remunerated and is often not considered as normal employment in accordance with labour law, with the result that women workers are subjected to unfair and unjustified treatment. very often, this work is done underground, and women workers, who come from rural areas or from abroad, are low-skilled, do not know their rights and become vulnerable. black-collar work robs workers of social protection and the community of income from taxes and social contributions. if we want to stop housework from being done in secret, we should make it a proper profession and overcome the stereotypes that often portray it as worthless. we should make it professional. however, this will require the introduction of new measures into the legal systems of the member states, in particular specific provisions in the fields of taxation, social security, labour and civil law, which take account of the specificities of the work thus performed. the current trend of offering and performing domestic work under the table is mostly economic, with both parties benefiting from the underground work rather than the officially registered work, which, in addition to taxes and fees, burdens both parties with extensive bureaucratic demands. the measures taken by the member states should therefore aim to change or even eliminate the benefits of undeclared work so that domestic work also becomes a specific form of decent work.
i would like to point out one fact that links veterinary medicine and human medicine. all the other european congresses of microbiologists, when they talked about antibiotic resistance in humans, they talked about what's called methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus. this is a plague that we in human medicine no longer have a valid antibiotic for, we can't cure it. up to 25,000 people a year die from it. please, how did this happen? the simply irresponsible use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine. they literally pump tons of antibiotics into the animals. in animals that are given it preventively, it is put in their food, and then it weakens the man and his ability to fight infection, perhaps in the hospital with such hospital strains. i would urge the commission to collect research from all member states urgently, but also to encourage new research into antibiotics that would be effective in humans and save lives.

rapporteur. − mr president, firstly i would like to thank all the honourable members concerned for their interesting input, and especially the shadow rapporteurs for their excellent cooperation. there were many inspiring and relevant ideas expressed in amendments, as well as in opinions, so i devoted special attention to creating a well-balanced approach that would capture as much of their essence and variety as possible. strategic reporting represents a new feature of cohesion policy, introduced in the current programming period 2007-2013. with the 2010 strategic report, parliament has the first occasion for analysis and evaluation of the outputs and results of cohesion policy implementation. this is also an opportunity to express parliament’s opinion on member states’ spending priorities, and to highlight areas where more efforts are needed, including the commission’s tackling of cohesion policy implementation and of the strategic reporting exercise itself. the 2010 strategic report focuses mainly on the implementation of programmes during the current programming period and the strategic reporting exercise. however, it also provides several valuable insights into the future of cohesion policy. firstly, regarding implementation of the programmes, the reported financial volume of the selected projects is eur 93.4 billion, representing more than 27% of available eu resources in the period in question. this can be considered quite reasonable, given not only the context of serious deterioration in the socio-economic situation in 2008-2009 due to the global crisis, but also the reform of the policy for the period 2007-2013. nevertheless, progress varies significantly between countries and across themes, with aggregate selection rates at about 40% in the case of nine member states and below 20% in four member states. striking economic, social and environmental disparities between the european regions clearly still exist. on the other hand, there was a more consistent average rate of project selection for the three objectives of convergence, regional competitiveness and employment and european territorial cooperation – and the same applies in the categories geared to the lisbon strategy objectives. the higher absorption rates for environmental programmes under the european territorial cooperation objective show the added value of cross-border and interregional cooperation – which should therefore be encouraged in future. on the other hand, more efforts are needed in certain areas, especially to improve implementation, avoid excessive delays, ensure tighter financial discipline and increase synergies with other eu policies. secondly, with regard to strategic reporting itself: this is a tool for reflecting strategically on, and discussing, the thematic dimension of cohesion policy on the basis of concrete evidence provided by member states. strategic reporting is also an evaluation of the ongoing process. it is carried out during the programming period in order to provide an overview of the member states’ progress in delivering on the eu’s goals, and a useful basis from which to improve performance. the report thus highlights many good practices capable of helping to enhance the quality of the reporting exercise, increasing ownership by stakeholders within the member states, and ultimately improving the efficiency of implementation. i will conclude by mentioning just one of the many good practices, namely the use of core indicators by all the member states.
rapporteur. − mr president, implementation of the programmes is a continuous and dynamic process that can be influenced by means of identifying frequent shortcomings in the whole process and areas where reforms are needed. in this context, strategic reporting, as a new instrument, increases accountability in delivering policy objectives and shows that cohesion policy should address all european regions and societal challenges in order to achieve smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in the whole eu. cohesion policy relies upon good governance at european, national, regional and local level. smooth cooperation at all these levels is as highly desirable as the simplification of the whole process. the funds must not, of course, remain unused owing to superfluous bureaucracy or onerous rules and procedures. well-financed cohesion policy should be closer to eu citizens and should continue to address all european union regions and societal challenges, both helping the poorer to catch up and delivering smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in the whole european union. the strategic report 2010 constitutes a strong incentive to improve the current implementation of the cohesion policy programmes. it also encourages the member states to correct delays in investing eu funds and to develop more efficient action plans to deliver the agreed results. therefore, i hope that the result of today’s vote on the strategic report 2010 will send that message to the member states and the commission.
in writing. cohesion policy after 2013 is to remain an important factor in the development of europe. it must guarantee the development of infrastructure and address disparities between regions. the financial crisis has deepened regional disparities. europe is facing high unemployment. at a time when there are more than 23 million unemployed, cohesion policy is one of the policies that can also contribute to job creation. there is probably no doubt among meps that cohesion policy will be needed beyond 2013. the question of the efficient use of funds, transparency and improvement of the whole process and return on investment is becoming topical. the successes of cohesion policy are measurable and are perceived and appreciated by eu citizens. it is therefore important that cohesion policy also has sufficient financial backing when adopting the future multiannual framework. investing in regional development is investing in the future and development of the eu.
the use of euro funds in new countries, including slovakia, is negatively affected by excessive complexity, excessive bureaucracy, unclear rules, but also hidden illicit interests. many who want to access money from european funds complain of a protracted bureaucratic torture with an uncertain end. the bureaucracy and many of the obstacles are not coming from brussels, but directly from the individual member states of the union. while european rules are being simplified under pressure from the european parliament, the rules introduced by individual member states often make the situation much more complicated. while the original european rules are relatively simple, national implementation complicates them. the rule is, the lower the organ, the more complicated the system gets. a major problem is that officials often do not help to draw on eu funds, but focus on checks that go far beyond what is required by law. the dog is therefore buried mainly in the member states of the european union.
the first decade of economic and monetary union has shown the need to improve the framework for economic governance. the new framework should be based on the enhanced responsibility of individual member states for commonly agreed rules and policies, as well as on a more robust framework for the supervision of national economic policies at union level. in particular, the experience of the last two years has confirmed that achieving strong competitiveness, sustainable economic growth and job availability requires sustainable public deficit and debt levels, reforms to address macroeconomic imbalances and a decisive eu strategy for growth and jobs. i have to admit some personal embarrassment over the introduction of administrative elements into economic mechanisms. on the other hand, experience so far shows that market mechanisms have failed to react in a timely and flexible manner to negative developments, with the consequence that the consequences of the financial crisis have turned into a debt crisis.
the current proposal by the european commission to reform the common agricultural policy is a cosmetic adjustment and not a reform aimed at improving the market or the competitiveness of european agricultural production. i also supported a number of the european parliament's conclusions and critical positions in this respect. i am firmly against the continuation of the historical approach in the subsidy system and i support the introduction of further objective criteria which will take account of the conditions for financing agriculture in the context of the enlarged european union of 27. i regard the so-called ceiling on subsidies as a complication which will not improve the conditions for farmers in the new member states. the common agricultural policy should be built on two pillars, the first pillar being fully financed by the european union. the second pillar must be geared to modernising agriculture, competitiveness and rural development with co-financing from national resources.
in writing. − in may 2011, the european council, together with the parliament, proposed the appointment of mario draghi as president of the european central bank for an eight-year term starting on 1 november 2011. the candidate was heard by the parliamentary committee on economic and monetary affairs and answered questions put by the committee members. he also commented on the greek debt problem and, inter alia, expressed the view that the ecb must not relax its efforts to maintain price stability. the committee subsequently recommended that draghi be appointed. since the candidate fulfils the requirements for the post of president of the ecb, i also express my support for his appointment to that post.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers who are feeling the effects of major structural changes in the world trade pattern. under the interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and sound financial management, the fund may not exceed a maximum annual amount of eur 500 million. in april 2011, the commission adopted a proposal to mobilise the fund for belgium in order to support the re-entry of workers into the labour market following redundancies caused by the global financial and economic crisis. the commission's assessment was based on an assessment of the link between the redundancies and significant structural changes in the world trade pattern or the financial crisis. in accordance with the commission's assessment, the application fulfils the eligibility criteria for financial support and i consider that it is appropriate to support the application. the european parliament, the council and the commission, in a joint statement, back in 2008, confirmed the importance of ensuring a rapid procedure for decisions on the mobilisation of the fund, with due regard to the interinstitutional agreement.
in writing. − in the previous parliamentary term, the conference of presidents set up a working group on parliamentary reform to review the functioning of parliament and propose improvements. in the chapter on inter-committee cooperation, the working party proposed not only to strengthen the position of the associated committee involved in the procedure of the associated committees, but also to develop a new form of inter-committee cooperation, based on the new article 51. this proposal was justified by the fact that in specific cases where a legislative document of major importance does not fall clearly within the remit of a single committee, it can also be split between several committees. and a dispute over jurisdiction is to be resolved according to the principles of equality and cooperation. the members of the committees concerned shall then vote jointly on the proposed amendments to the legislative proposal. and the plenary is then presented with the more balanced report. i think that the interpretation of the rules of procedure or the guidelines is not sufficient to facilitate the implementation of the procedure. this is an important procedural question which must be decided by a majority vote in the plenary. it is desirable to achieve greater clarity of the provision and thus its applicability.

in writing. −the bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and the seychelles was signed in 1987 and the fisheries partnership agreement has been in force since 2006. the economy of seychelles is based mainly on tourism and fishing, with the fish-preserving industry accounting for 15% of gdp and employing 17% of the local working population. the commission, acting under the relevant council mandate and on behalf of the european union, negotiated with the republic of seychelles with a view to renewing the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles. the agreement is mutually beneficial for both the eu and seychelles, and has created 2 900 jobs in seychelles and 760 jobs in europe in fisheries-related jobs. the agreement provides for a qualitative improvement in the multiannual sectoral programme to promote responsible and sustainable fishing in seychelles' waters and also includes a suspension clause in the protocol, which allows the agreement to be suspended if one of the parties proves that there has been a violation of human rights. the agreement contributes significantly to the stabilisation of the european market, the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the rational use of fishery resources in the seychelles' fishing zone. it is therefore appropriate to approve the draft new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the seychelles.
in writing. − the negotiation and conclusion of fisheries partnership agreements responds to the general objective of preserving and protecting the activities of the european union fishing fleet, including the fishing fleet in remote areas, and developing relations in the spirit of partnership and cooperation with third countries in order to enhance the sustainable use of fisheries resources outside eu waters, taking into account environmental, social and economic issues. to this end, the european council adopted a regulation in july 2007 on the conclusion of a fisheries partnership agreement between the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe and the european community. the fisheries agreement with são tomé and príncipe not only responds to the needs of the european fleet, but can also contribute to supporting the viability of the eu tuna fishing sector in the atlantic ocean. the fisheries of são tomé and príncipe are mainly concentrated on coastal resources, with about 15% of the active population still dependent on fishing for their livelihood. the proposal in question is in the interests of both parties and therefore it is not appropriate to approve it.
in writing. − the council decision submitted to the european parliament under the assent procedure constitutes the legal instrument for the conclusion of a protocol between the european union and the principality of andorra extending the scope of the agreement on customs security measures. the agreement served as the basis for a customs union between the two parties. the community customs code can in principle be applied to trade with all non-member countries, but it allows the application of other rules in cases where international agreements provide for specific security measures. the protocol is intended to ensure that trade between the two parties involved is conducted without complications and at a high level of customs security and to include a set of rules to ensure that the agreement remains consistent with the eu acquis. i therefore believe that it is appropriate for parliament to give its consent to the agreement. at the same time, however, although relations between the eu and the principality of andorra have developed, they are fragmented, with significant parts of the internal market acquis not incorporated into andorran law and thus not applicable. it is therefore necessary to analyse as soon as possible the possibilities and ways of possible gradual integration into the internal market.
in writing. − the recommendation concerns the security agreement signed on behalf of the european community in may 2009. canada has been duly considered as a priority for the conclusion of an aviation safety agreement to complement the air transport agreement, as both europe and canada are home to world-leading aircraft, engine and avionics manufacturers. as with the similar aviation safety agreement with the united states, the main objective was to minimise the duplication of assessments, tests and inspections and to allow the eu and canada to rely on each other's certification systems. the agreement thus broadly follows the structure of existing bilateral aviation safety agreements concluded between the member states and canada. it shall impose obligations and establish methods of cooperation, be based on mutual trust in each other's systems and on the comparison of regulatory differences. european and canadian companies will save millions of euros a year through shorter, simpler and less costly product approval procedures and mutual recognition of certification findings. it will also benefit airlines and also represent a significant step forward in terms of establishing international standards in the field of civil aviation safety. i therefore believe that it is appropriate for parliament to give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement, as this will also make both the canadian and european markets more competitive and also more secure.
in writing. − the implementation reports analyse the implementation of eu legislation in national law and its enforcement in the member states. in the case of cohesion policy, the legislative framework consists of directly applicable regulations. the commission report entitled 'cohesion policy: strategic report 2010 on the implementation of the 2007-2013 programmes' thus analyses whether member states have properly applied the legislation and how member states have understood and followed the community strategic guidelines when implementing national strategic reference frameworks and operational programmes. cohesion policy is proving to be important as it makes a significant contribution to improving the socio-economic environment. member states are making progress towards achieving its objectives, as evidenced by the facts and figures presented in the national reports. however, sound financial discipline and transparency in the allocation of funds are, of course, essential prerequisites for the achievement of the overall objectives of cohesion policy. strategic reporting as a new tool can make a significant contribution to increasing accountability in meeting policy objectives in this respect. similarly, steps to simplify the management and implementation of cohesion policy remain highly desirable and justified in order to achieve the policy's objectives and thus contribute to european solidarity.
in writing. − the report addresses several aspects of the urban dimension of cohesion policy which the committee on regional development considers to be key or problematic for the future cohesion policy, which is to become a full-fledged and effective policy for eu cities. europe is characterised by territorial diversity and polycentric development, with few large cities within a relatively dense urban network. a strengthened urban agenda requires the development and qualitative modernisation of infrastructure and services in european cities. it is desirable that future actions are closely linked to the overall eu priorities. although european cities are centres of economic activity, innovation and employment, they face a number of challenges that require an individual approach to address them, taking into account local needs. european regional and cohesion policy addresses this issue. the problems encountered need to be addressed in an integrated manner at eu, national and regional level and funding options coordinated in a way that covers a wide range of specific needs.
in writing. − the importance of territorial cooperation has increased considerably in recent years, due to the general regulation on the structural funds and the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it aims to remove physical, administrative and regulatory barriers and to mitigate the so-called border effect between territories and regions, so that they can respond as a whole to common challenges. the balance between the three basic components cross-border cooperation, transnational cooperation and interregional cooperation must be maintained, as each has its own justification and benefits. in order to fulfil the principle of territorial cohesion, it is necessary to better complement the objective of territorial cooperation and the common procedures. for its successful implementation and development, territorial cooperation as an important european idea should also be a kind of symbolic embodiment of the eu for all citizens.
in writing. − europe is in a post-crisis period and therefore even more efforts are needed to coordinate the activities of eu funds and programmes. as regards the european social fund, experience has shown that the financing of economic measures by the european regional development fund can be more effective if it is better coordinated and integrated with the activities carried out by the fund. it should be borne in mind that the good outcome of most programmes and measures depends to a large extent on a successful combination of several factors, the most important of which is human development. the current system of planning and implementation of programmes, which links policies relating to human resources development, business development, especially smes, or, for example, infrastructure development, serves as a tool for bringing the assisted regions closer together. each of these policies would achieve less on its own than all of them together currently do under an integrated system of programming and implementation. however, i believe that an even more extensive coordination mechanism is needed to help bring instruments, policies and stakeholders into line. it is desirable that carefully planned interventions and programmes are implemented and take into account the local specificities and comparative advantages or specificities of each region within an integrated approach based on local specificities.
in writing. − the efforts to correct macroeconomic imbalances are of paramount importance for the future of the euro area and the eu. parliament intends to improve the commission's proposals in order to create a strong and coherent framework for the coming decades, guaranteeing the compatibility of fiscal discipline with the objectives of economic growth and employment in the union and in all member states, since only the fulfilment of this condition will ensure the stability and sustainability of the union and the euro. strengthening the governance of economic affairs must be complemented appropriately by strengthening the democratic legitimacy of the decisions taken. this requires closer and earlier involvement of not only the relevant stakeholders but also, and in particular, of national parliaments and the european parliament in the whole process. it is appropriate that the stability and growth pact and the full economic governance framework appropriately support and are consistent with the union's strategies for growth and jobs, and also aim to enhance the competitiveness of all member states and social stability in all regions of the union. the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances is an effective tool to address weaknesses arising in particular from medium- and long-term structural trends, growing disparities within the union and the euro area, and the external implications of the policies of individual member states. it is desirable to improve the framework for economic governance and thus contribute to sustainable and balanced growth in the union as a whole.
in writing. − the global economic and financial crisis has revealed and deepened the need for closer coordination and better surveillance of economic policies in the economic and monetary union. the existing instruments and procedures for coordination and surveillance have enabled the eu to overcome a crisis that no member state could have overcome on its own. the european institutions and the member states are working together to recover from the crisis. however, this experience has revealed shortcomings and weaknesses in the current system of coordination and in the existing supervisory procedures. it is essential to strengthen the framework of economic and monetary union in order to consolidate macroeconomic stability and the sustainability of public finances, which are prerequisites for sustained performance and employment growth. the various elements of economic policy coordination, including the surveillance of structural reforms, need to be integrated into a new surveillance cycle, the so-called european semester, which links the existing processes under the pact with the broad economic policy guidelines and ensures the simultaneous submission of stabilisation and convergence programmes and national reform programmes.
in writing. − the global economic and financial crisis has sharply reversed the favourable economic and financial conditions that prevailed until 2007, and has once again highlighted that the windfall accumulated in the good times has not been sufficiently used to create room for purposeful action in the bad times. the availability of fiscal data is essential for the proper functioning of the union budgetary surveillance framework. timely and reliable fiscal data are essential for proper and well-timed monitoring, which allows prompt action to be taken in the event of an adverse budgetary situation. transparency, which must include regular availability of the fiscal data, is an essential element in ensuring the quality of the data.
in writing. − in june 2010, the european council agreed that it was urgent to strengthen the coordination of our economic policies. this agreement included in particular the stability and growth pact (sgp) and budgetary surveillance. this was mainly to strengthen the preventive and corrective parts of the psr and to ensure that all member states had national budgetary rules and medium-term budgetary frameworks in line with the psr. member states whose currency is the euro have a particular interest in and responsibility for pursuing economic policies which promote the proper functioning of economic and monetary union and for seeking to prevent the application of policies which threaten it. sanctions for member states whose currency is the euro should provide incentives for prudent fiscal policy-making in the preventive part of the psr. at the same time, room for budgetary manoeuvre is also preserved, taking into account in particular the necessity for public investment.
in writing. − the recent economic and financial crisis has revealed and deepened the need for better coordination and increased surveillance of economic policies in the economic and monetary union. there are still gaps and weaknesses in the current system of coordination and in the existing supervisory procedures. the framework for economic and monetary union should therefore also be urgently strengthened in order to anchor macroeconomic stability and the sustainability of public finances. most member states will necessarily need substantial consolidation to return to the downward trend in public debt. but the problems are all the more pressing as european societies and economies face the consequences of an ageing population, which may put even greater pressure on labour supply and public finance budgets. the coordination of the economic policies of the member states within the european union should include, in particular, the maintenance of a sustainable balance of payments and the need for public investment.
in writing. − the existence of large macroeconomic imbalances, including large and persistent differences in competitiveness trends, proved to be very damaging to the european union at the time of the crisis, especially with regard to the euro. the low cost of financing in the years before the crisis led to an improper allocation of resources, often allocated to less productive purposes, resulting in unsustainable consumption rates in some member states, the emergence of real estate bubbles and the accumulation of both external and internal debt. it is therefore important to establish a new structured procedure to prevent and remedy undesirable macroeconomic imbalances in all member states. the europe 2020 strategy sets out an ambitious and comprehensive strategy to ensure smart, sustainable and inclusive growth of the european union economy. in the context of the crisis, this strategy identifies new areas to focus on in addressing europe's weaknesses in the surveillance of macro-financial and structural challenges. it calls for the development of a specific policy framework for the euro area to address wider macroeconomic imbalances, and in particular takes into account the deep economic and financial links within the euro area and their impact on the single currency. for this reason, i believe that a mechanism to monitor the sources of macroeconomic imbalances and to ensure that appropriate corrective measures are taken, where necessary, is essential, with a key focus on the link between preventive and corrective measures.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to ensure that consumers in all 27 eu member states can rely on a high level of consumer protection and that businesses of all sizes are able to supply goods and services to consumers in all 27 eu member states without unnecessary legal obstacles. the fragmentation of existing legislation is deterring consumers and businesses considering engaging in cross-border trade. consumers often complain that they cannot fully benefit from the single market, as traders with operations in another member state are often not prepared to comply with the different provisions applicable in that market when entering a new market, and moreover they also refuse to open up to possible legal action in another member state. the possible solution to the difficulties encountered appears to be to change the scope of the proposed directive, whereby, in addition to introducing a series of sectoral derogations, the scope of the directive would be significantly limited to off-premises contracts, which account for the largest proportion of cross-border transactions. i therefore consider it desirable to apply an approach aimed at full and comprehensive harmonisation limited to specific aspects of certain contracts while maintaining a high level of consumer protection.
in writing. − the directive in question concerns emissions from agricultural tractors and aims to amend directive 2000/25/ec by a quantitative amendment. this directive is urgent in that it affects a period which has already started on 1 january 2011 and is of great importance in view of its expected positive effects on the sector concerned. for each type of tractor, the directive sets a maximum emission level based on engine power and provides for a gradual reduction of emissions in several stages. the limits set for the stage that has just begun are much stricter than for the previous stage. in order to facilitate the transition between these stages, the directive introduces a system of flexibility allowing tractor manufacturers to place on the market a limited number of tractors with engines calibrated to the emission limits permitted during the previous stage. the commission's proposed directive is to be strongly welcomed. it takes account of environmental objectives that the eu has already agreed to. if the proposed amendment were not adopted, paradoxically we would end up with the exact opposite result, as many farmers could choose to keep their old polluting tractors, thus worsening the environment in europe. i therefore think it is desirable to support the amendment of the directive, since its adoption would achieve the objective of protecting the environment or, in the same way, promote the economic prospects of the industry concerned.
in writing. − the commission published a proposal for a directive last november setting out the eu legal framework for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. the proposal sets out specific requirements to ensure the safe handling and disposal of spent fuel and radioactive waste from its generation to its storage. the principle of reversibility should be duly taken into account in the design and technical solution of the final disposal, in particular the deep geological disposal of spent fuel and highly radioactive waste. the aim is to enable potential access to and recovery of waste, whether for technical reasons or where advances in research make room for new longer-term technological solutions. however, the landfilling of waste must in all circumstances be carried out in accordance with internationally accepted safety standards, requirements and methodologies. ultimately, it is the responsibility of the member states to ensure the safe management of the spent fuel and radioactive waste they generate, including its safe storage. and while it is crucial that each member state develops its own national programme for spent fuel and radioactive waste, the alternative of finding common solutions to the issue may also be of interest. however, i am of the opinion that such a concept cannot, under any circumstances, be a substitute for encouraging member states to avoid their national obligations relating to the management of radioactive waste.

the unregulated derivatives trade was undoubtedly one of the factors that led to the financial crisis. i therefore consider the draft regulation to be crucial to preventing further crises. the lack of transparency of derivatives makes it impossible to identify the nature and extent of the risk and thus threatens financial stability and society as a whole. in this respect, the establishment of the european securities and markets authority and its role in assessing which derivatives are to be cleared is important. the functioning of this body should continue to be supported as it reduces systemic risk in the financial system, including the potential failure of highly connected counterparties to meet their payment obligations. however, in this context i would like to call on the commission, commissioner, to pay particular attention to the trading of financial institutions in commodity markets. the involvement of financiers is already apparently unhealthy and therefore the commission should consider whether participation in commodity exchanges should not be limited to physical traders.
like today's derivatives debate, the discussion of short selling and credit default swaps is important for preserving already fragile financial stability. it is essential that those provisions take the form of a regulation since they impose direct obligations on private parties to disclose information. transparency is necessary in particular for reasons of stability in financial markets and investor protection. another important point in this proposal is the proposal to ban so-called uncovered short selling. the current debt crisis shows how speculators, who do not even own the bonds of eurozone member states but only bet on them, can bring about the collapse of entire states. it is therefore important that only bondholders can engage in the insurance of securities through credit default swaps. the final important agenda of the text presented is to strengthen the powers of esma. i hope that the council will reconsider its position that it should be the finance ministers, and not esma, who decide in so-called exceptional situations, and that esma will be given priority in this regard.
