in writing. − export controls on dual-use items, i.e. goods that can be used for both civilian and military purposes, have been the subject of eu-level measures for some 15 years. the control of exports of dual-use items is of key importance in terms of non-proliferation of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. the main eu instrument in the field of export controls is regulation (ec) no 428/2009 on dual-use items, which entered into force on 27 august 2009 and introduces several significant changes to the scope of export controls on dual-use items. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which clarifies the union's powers in international trade, provides a good opportunity to reaffirm the eu's role in these groupings and the role, powers and responsibilities of the european parliament within the eu's institutional decision-making framework. the eu regime for dual-use items should be more transparent and democratic. i believe that the full involvement of the european parliament through the implementation of the obligations arising from the treaty of lisbon and its common interpretation, agreed by the european parliament and the european commission on the basis of the new framework agreement, should be essential to achieve this objective.

in writing. − i am pleased that the report draws attention to the interconnectedness of two seemingly completely different european policies: development and agriculture. because the huge food subsidies for european union producers contribute significantly to food and agricultural labour shortages in developing countries in africa, asia and the caribbean. if you pay five times less for milk from the netherlands than you do for milk from a local producer in the gambia today, and for dutch potatoes at a quarter of the price a gambian farmer is able to deliver them to the market, something is wrong. these price differences are not the result of the higher productivity of the dutch producers. these are the results of european subsidies policy. first, we contribute from our taxes to our producers to push local producers out of the markets in developing countries, and then we give alms to those countries in the form of development aid. the result: we pay twice as much, and people in the gambia feel that their efforts are going nowhere anyway. there's a way to help developing countries quickly and effectively.
in writing. − the report was drawn up at the request of the conference of committee chairs to the committee on constitutional affairs, with a view to clarifying parliament's position on the meaning and legal effect of unilateral statements recorded in the minutes of council meetings. several committee chairs expressed concern at the increase in such declarations, especially in the context of the codecision procedure, where they could weaken the legal force and scope of adopted legislation and thus affect parliament's role as co-legislator. in that regard, it should be noted that the statements at issue come primarily from one or more member states, since the latter are responsible for transposing the legislation at national level. indeed, attempting to interpret that legislation in a way which might differ from the objective pursued by the mutual agreement of the two legislative bodies would undermine the necessary coherence in the application of union legislation. the case-law of the court of justice confirms that such unilateral statements are not to be relied upon in the interpretation of union law. for this purpose, statements may be used only if the wording of the relevant legislation refers to their content. as a co-legislator with the same status as the council, parliament should also be informed of the unilateral statements made by member states which are recorded in the minutes of council meetings, at all stages of the legislative procedure.
in writing. − in the co-decision procedure, unilateral statements recorded in the minutes of council meetings weaken the legal force of adopted legislation. in doing so, they can influence parliament's role as co-legislator. the declarations at issue come primarily from one or more member states, since the states are responsible for transposing the legislation at national level. the treaty of lisbon provides for the direct transmission of the minutes of the legislative part of council meetings to the member states and national parliaments, as amended by the council's rules of procedure. there is no mention of the european parliament. this gives the national parliaments an advantage over the european parliament, even though it is the council's co-legislator. unilateral statements by member states concerning legislation should not be published in the official journal of the european union. it is necessary to prevent references to unilateral declarations and to ensure that the council provides parliament with complete information during all stages of the legislative procedure.

mr president, on 29 september 2010 the commission presented a legislative package aimed at strengthening economic governance in the eu and the euro area. the package consists of six proposals. four of these are on fiscal issues, including the reform of the stability and growth pact, while two new regulations relate to the detection and management of macroeconomic imbalances in the eu and the euro area. the latter two proposals contain new elements. the preventive part of these elements involves the regular assessment of the risk of imbalances based on a scoreboard of indicators and the carrying out of detailed country analyses. the corrective arm envisages that euro area member states that do not comply adequately with the recommendations applicable to them may be subject to excessive deficit procedures and ultimately to annual financial penalties. the imbalance adjustment system should include not only sanctions but also incentives. the fines collected from non-compliant member states should be used for the eu's long-term investment and employment objectives. i was happy to support the report.

in writing. − australia has the right to restore its trade rights, which have been slightly distorted as a result of the eu customs union enlargement with romania and bulgaria. the objective of a customs union or a free trade area should be to facilitate trade between the territories which constitute it, and not to create obstacles to trade between the other contracting parties and those territories. this agreement is another sign that the eu is willing to abide by the rules of the multilateral trading system and to participate in the collective readiness to reach a comprehensive agreement in the doha development round. the commission has rightly chosen the extension of the tariff quotas of the products concerned to australia as the compensation instrument, as this is the most targeted way of providing compensation to a country which has become eligible for compensation. although the commission has not carried out a proper impact assessment, research and stakeholder dialogue confirm that this agreement will not harm the eu's agricultural interests as it will restore australia's pre-existing rights.
in writing. − the commission has rightly chosen the extension of the tariff quotas for the new zealand products concerned as the compensation instrument, as this is the most targeted way of providing compensation to a country that deserves compensation. although the commission has not carried out a proper impact assessment, research and stakeholder dialogue confirm that this agreement will not harm the eu's agricultural interests as it will only restore new zealand's pre-existing rights. the eu and new zealand shall notify each other of the completion of their internal procedures necessary for the entry into force of the agreement. it is to be hoped that our partner country will also end its internal procedures without delay so that producers can soon reap the benefits of market access.
in writing. − with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the eu has enlarged its customs union. as a result, the eu was obliged under wto rules to enter into negotiations with wto members, who have the right to negotiate within the framework of the commitments lists of the acceding members, with a view to agreeing on a compensatory settlement. the aim is to reach a mutually satisfactory settlement to compensate for the increase in the level of the duties being imposed. both sides have an interest in reaching an agreement. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations under article xxiv:6 of gatt with countries entitled to compensation. the agreement with new zealand was initialled on 7 september 2010. the council approved the signing of the agreement on 11 april 2011. the agreement with new zealand was signed on 28 april 2011. in order to meet wto requirements, these agreements address two issues. the first is the compensation of higher duties which must be compensated, the second is the fact that the pre-accession tariff quota of bulgaria and romania must also be added to the existing eu tariff quota applied to all. i welcome the agreement with new zealand and i am of the opinion that the european parliament should give its consent. new zealand has the right to restore its trade rights, which have been slightly weakened as a result of the eu customs union enlargement to romania and bulgaria.
in writing. − the coordination of the economic policies of the member states within the eu should include adherence to the guiding principles of price stability, sound public finances and monetary conditions, and a sustainable balance of payments. the stability and growth pact aims at sound public finances as a means of strengthening the conditions for price stability and strong sustainable growth contributing to job creation. the preventive arm of the stability and growth pact requires member states to achieve and maintain a medium-term budgetary objective and to submit stability and convergence programmes to that end. the achievement of the medium-term budgetary objective of budgetary position should allow member states to create a safe-harbour with a 3% of gdp reference value in order to ensure rapid progress towards sustainability and to gain room for budgetary manoeuvre, in particular with regard to public investment needs. the obligation to achieve and maintain the medium-term budgetary objective must be implemented by defining prudent fiscal policy-making principles. in order to maintain compliance with the fiscal surveillance framework, a specific enforcement mechanism should be established for cases where there is a persistent and significant deviation from prudent fiscal policy-making. the references in regulation (ec) no 1466/97 need to take account of the new numbering of the articles in the treaty on the functioning of the european union and i therefore consider that this regulation should be amended accordingly.
in writing. − if you have the experience gained during the first decade of the functioning of the economic and monetary union, as well as the mistakes made during that period, indicate the need to improve the economic governance of the union, which should be based on greater responsibility for commonly agreed rules and policies by the individual member states and a stronger framework for the surveillance of national economic policies at union level. this regulation will make it possible to issue recommendations and require interest-bearing deposits from those member states that do not comply with their medium-term fiscal consolidation targets, even if their results were in line with the rules of the stability and growth pact (3% deficit, 60% debt). i did not support the regulation because: (1) it does not analyse how such economic policy management will contribute to the europe 2020 strategy; such rules will result in the objectives of long-term growth, modernisation and sustainability having to be subjected to short-term budgetary and market pressures; (2) the rules are not based on economic theory and will tie the hands of politicians; (3) the regulation favours cuts in spending over revenue growth; it thus hinders growth, employment and contributes to the dismantling of the state.

in writing. − the global economic and financial crisis has revealed and deepened the need for closer coordination and better surveillance of economic policies in the economic and monetary union. the existing instruments and methods of coordination and surveillance have enabled the eu to overcome a crisis that no member state could have overcome on its own. the european institutions and the member states have responded swiftly and continue to work together to recover from a crisis unprecedented in our generation. the member states whose currency is the euro have a particular interest in and responsibility for pursuing economic policies that promote the proper functioning of economic and monetary union and for avoiding policies that threaten it. the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and in particular article 136 thereof, in conjunction with article 121 (6) thereof, allows for specific measures to be adopted in the euro area, going beyond the provisions applicable to all member states, in order to ensure the proper functioning of economic and monetary union. further sanctions are necessary to enhance the effectiveness of fiscal surveillance in the euro area and should provide incentives for prudent fiscal policy-making. this would allow the medium-term budgetary objective to be effectively achieved and maintained and ensure rapid progress towards sustainability, while maintaining room for budgetary manoeuvre, in particular in view of the need for public investment.

in writing. − the six legislative proposals adopted by the commission last september as part of a package to ensure the coherence of all legislative texts are of particular importance for the future of the eu and in particular the euro area. parliament intends to improve the commission's proposals in order to create a strong and coherent framework for the coming decades, guaranteeing compatibility between fiscal discipline and the objectives of economic growth and employment in the union and in all member states. only this condition will ensure the stability and sustainability of the union and the euro. this call comes at a particularly difficult time for the union and the euro area, which are facing tensions in growth, employment and internal divisions, which are being seriously exacerbated by a serious international crisis, but it is also an appropriate time to change, supplement and rectify the existing model in the light of past and current knowledge. this is the first time that parliament has co-decided with the council on macroeconomic developments and fiscal discipline in the union. strengthening the governance of economic affairs must go hand in hand with strengthening the democratic legitimacy of decisions taken, which requires closer and more timely involvement not only of the relevant stakeholders, but in particular of national parliaments and the european parliament, in the whole process, for the sustainable and balanced growth of the union as a whole. that is why i am in favour of a comprehensive reform of the governance framework based on the community (union) method.

in writing. − this regulation sets out recommendations, warnings and, ultimately, sanctions for those euro area member states that do not comply with the rules of the stability and growth pact on a 3% deficit and 60% debt ratio. the logic of the regulation is the same as that of the report on the preventive instrument of the pact (wortmann-kool), and therefore suffers from the same shortcomings. as a result, the objectives of long-term growth, modernisation and sustainability will have to be subject to short-term budgetary and market pressures. the regulation is based on a politically biased concept of budgetary consolidation, which favours cuts in expenditure over increases in budgetary revenue. in this way, it contributes to the dismantling of the state. that's why i voted against it.

the use of body scanners has undoubtedly its advantages and can contribute to the improvement of aviation safety. one of the positives is that they can detect not only metal objects. this is a plus in an age where potential weapons are made up of components made from different materials. however, the scanning method must be acceptable from the point of view of the protection of the privacy of the travelling public. only schematic images shall be available and any data thus obtained shall be destroyed immediately after the person has passed the security check. at the same time, it is equally important to exclude any radiation or effects that could endanger the health of passengers. the scanning itself should be carried out by random selection and any rejection should not automatically lead to suspicion. however, if the passenger refuses the check, he must undergo an alternative type of security check that guarantees the same level of security.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to support measures for workers who have been most severely affected by the mass redundancies caused by globalisation or by the financial and economic crisis in the european union, in order to support their reintegration into the labour market. it was designed as a rapid intervention tool in the event of mass redundancies in order to prevent long-term unemployment in difficult labour market conditions. its original aim as a tool was to alleviate as quickly as possible the urgent and unforeseen problems in the labour market caused by the large number of redundancies, whether from large firms or small enterprises operating in a certain sector and a certain region. i also think it is important to stress that in the future, the main focus should be on sustainable labour market measures and our efforts should be to create the conditions for member states to use the egf to meet european objectives and to support new skills, including those related to new, sustainable, and high-quality 'green' jobs. similarly, the egf should continue to finance only those active labour market measures which are complementary to the measures under national legislation for mass redundancies and i think it would be appropriate for the commission to monitor the implementation process in more detail in order to ensure that the measures have the same beneficial effects on all workers.
in writing. − if you have the objective of the review was to broaden the scope of the egf in europe's response to the crisis and to transform it into a more timely and effective instrument for intervention in times of crisis, in line with the fundamental principles of solidarity and social justice. the amendments included, for example, reducing the number of redundancies required to apply for egf support from 1 000 to 500 workers and extending the period of implementation of measures supported by the egf from 12 to 24 months. a temporary derogation was introduced to: 1. extend the scope of the egf to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the financial and economic crisis; 2. increase the co-financing rate applicable to the egf from 50% to 65%. the temporary derogation is to expire on 30 december 2011. during the consultation carried out by the commission, member states indicated that without the temporary derogation, most of the applications related to the crisis could not be submitted, i.e. approximately 45 000 workers who have suffered the adverse effects of the economic and financial crisis would be left without support from the egf.

i am not from romania or bulgaria, but i would like to ask the honourable member, since i did not have the opportunity to ask the previous honourable member, mr van daalen, although i do not represent these two countries: where do you find the right to judge the member states of the european union which have fulfilled all the necessary conditions to become part of the schengen area, to address them in the european parliament in the way you do? are your countries better off compared to other eu member states that are in schengen?
real solutions based on facts must be promoted through political decisions. so, first, the facts. romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis when they joined the union in 2007. both countries have substantially reworked and reorganised their integrated border management systems and have significantly strengthened their institutional and legal frameworks. this is recognised in all schengen evaluation reports. both countries have fully implemented the schengen acquis, which is the only condition for their accession to the schengen area under the accession treaty and the current legal framework of the european union. finally, in its resolution adopted in june this year, parliament confirmed by a large majority that romania and bulgaria were ready to join. i therefore call on all member states to take a decision to extend the schengen area to these two countries solely on the basis of the schengen acquis and the schengen procedures currently in force. i am of the opinion that member states already in the process of joining the schengen area cannot be subject to additional criteria. it is therefore appropriate for the competent authorities to take the necessary measures to allow romania and bulgaria to accede to the schengen area, as they have fulfilled the list of requirements which were given to those countries when they signed the treaty of accession.
the schengen area is one of the most tangible manifestations of freedom of movement in the european union for citizens. romania and bulgaria, as member states, have the right to become members of this area as any other country of the union. their entry standards and criteria must be the same as for any other country. the latest assessment by the schengen evaluation working group showed that both countries fulfil the criteria for schengen entry and have implemented the schengen acquis in all seven required areas. as with any other measure, the principles and values on which the union is founded must be respected. equal access to the rights and obligations of individual member states and the facilitation of the free movement of persons is one of them. the member states and the european institutions should be aware that the use of double meters is inadmissible in this situation. i therefore call on the council and the polish presidency to start addressing this issue as soon as possible.
in writing i would like to express my deep concern at the low level of solidarity with bulgaria and romania. just like in sports, in business or politics, the rules don't change during the game. these countries have fulfilled the necessary requirements of the accession treaties and are ready to join the common schengen area, as already demonstrated by the report adopted in june. i therefore share the same position as most of my colleagues across the political spectrum: a double standard for old and new member states is not acceptable. such interference with the rules would increase mistrust in the schengen acquis and at the same time create a dangerous precedent that could have a profound impact on future member states. i would therefore like to express my support for romania and bulgaria and at the same time call on the countries blocking their entry into schengen to reconsider their position.

the financial crisis has shown that consumer confidence in the financial system can be quickly eroded. this is particularly the case where adequate procedures are not available to compensate for the losses suffered by consumers as a result of the failure of financial institutions. insurance guarantee schemes can be a valuable tool in reducing the risks to which insured persons are exposed should an insurance company fail and become insolvent. however, these insurance guarantee schemes often differ in terms of cover. this then leads to different degrees of protection for insured persons in the various member states. there are also significant differences in other aspects affecting the extent of protection provided, as well as in operating procedures and financing methods. in order to maintain consumer confidence in the insurance industry, but also in the single market for financial services, a uniform level of consumer protection should, in my view, be ensured. the consumer should, so to speak, be assured that all types of insurance products he purchases are covered by insurance guarantee schemes and that these schemes will guarantee that he will receive 100% of the reimbursement at the specified time, which will be uniform throughout the european union.
the upcoming implementation of the solvency ii directive from 2013 will have a significant impact on the european insurance market. however, as it stands, this directive does not protect consumers from losses in cases of insurance company default and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection therefore recommends that the commission bring the insurance guarantee scheme into line with that directive. a single, legally binding framework for the protection of insurance guarantee schemes based on minimum harmonisation appears to be a good starting point. in particular, in relation to the cross-border activities of insurers, certain problems may arise in countries without insurance guarantee schemes. the european union does not have harmonised consumer protection standards, so providers operating in more than one national system would have to expect higher costs under the host country approach. therefore, the home country principle appears to be a more advantageous alternative to cover the larger geographical scope of the insurance guarantee scheme. however, the commission should use the remaining time to assess the open issues so that the required objectives are achieved when the solvency ii directive enters into force.
the diversity of insurance guarantee schemes in the european union is due to the specificities of the national markets in the member states. however, the diversity creates considerable uncertainty for consumers, especially in cross-border cases where it is not clear from the statutes which rules will apply. the insurance guarantee scheme at european level needs to guarantee more effective protection for all eu insured persons and should therefore also include the establishment of appropriate procedures for compensation for consumers who have suffered losses as a result of the failure of financial institutions. the proposal for a directive on insurance guarantee schemes should improve the existing system of deposit protection and thus contribute to creating more homogeneous conditions in the internal insurance market. in my view, ensuring that consumers are equally protected regardless of the country of residence of the insurer and improving consumer awareness of the risks associated with the provision of financial services remains a clear priority.
for the s&d group within the framework of the competences shared between the european union and the member states, the principle of subsidiarity lays down the conditions under which the union may act on behalf of the member states. in addition to areas falling within the exclusive competence of the european union, the principle of subsidiarity is understood to protect the decision-making capacity and the action of the member states, on the one hand, and to justify union intervention where the objectives of the action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states, on the other. the involvement of national parliaments following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, in particular protocol no 2, is the subject of an annual report submitted by the commission. the report deals with issues such as the subsidiarity principles put into practice by institutions such as the european commission, parliament, council and committee of the regions. it also deals with the subsidiarity mechanism of national parliaments, which was one of the anticipated innovations implemented with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. in my view, mr vice-president, it is appropriate to focus attention on some of the issues raised in the area and in the issue of subsidiarity. the european parliament has been defending the concept of subsidiarity for many years. since 1 december 2009, member states' parliaments have had the possibility to inform the president of the european commission, in a reasoned opinion, that they consider that the proposed legislative procedures are not in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. i would therefore be interested, mr vice-president, to hear the commission's view on this matter: what has it done and how has it addressed the european parliament's requests?
value added tax is one of the most important revenues for the countries of the european union. however, cross-border trade is subject to a high level of tax evasion and it is therefore appropriate to look for ways to improve current mechanisms for recording and reporting and collecting value added tax. tax policy is a competence of the member states and therefore the union's initiatives in this area are very limited. nevertheless, we find in mr cass's report a number of suggestions for improving the current rules. a vat system built on a broad basis, as defined by the oecd, can provide a good basis for further coordinated improvement of the recording and collection mechanisms for cross-border transactions. another benefit may be the effort made to reduce red tape. simplifying reporting, reducing the frequency of declarations, making better use of e-government and introducing a european invoice based on a language-neutral template will certainly help tax authorities and businesses. i am convinced that any simplification and transparency of the system will contribute to a better collection of this tax.
after more than 40 years since the introduction of vat, the value added tax, it is indeed high time to review this system. the aim should be to enhance its compatibility with the single market and its contribution to other policies. vat reform can play a crucial role in supporting the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and the return to economic growth through its potential to re-energize the single market and to promote smart budget consolidation in the member states. all such improvements require a complete vat system that can adapt to changes in the economic and technological environment. simplifying the vat system would also reduce the operational costs of taxpayers and tax administrations, thus increasing net revenue to the treasury. the cost of ensuring compliance with vat rules is a relatively large administrative burden for eu businesses and its reduction would greatly contribute to increasing their competitiveness. finally, the last sentence: it is essential to find solutions so that money, including vat, does not flow from the budgets of the member states to so-called tax havens.
written value added tax is the most important item in each state budget, therefore no tax evasion can be accepted. the differences in vat rates between member states are exploited for various fraudulent purposes, particularly in cross-border transactions. every day in our member states we can meet illegal traders who sell goods imported from other countries directly on the street, without receiving a document, without a cash register, and even the mayors of the villages announce this sale on the local radio. the regulatory authorities turn a blind eye to such phenomena. in addition to these 'small' frauds, larger, more sophisticated ones, with hundreds of thousands of frauds, are uncovered every year. it is therefore high time to introduce a single european tax and uniform control mechanisms. the economic crisis has revealed shortcomings in the collection and control of individual taxes, and vat is one of the most important.

in writing − insurance guarantee schemes are used as a last resort to protect consumers when insurers are unable to meet their contractual obligations. in this way, they protect citizens against the risk of non-payment of their claims in the event of insolvency of their insurance companies. however, they often differ in cover, resulting in different degrees of protection for insured persons between member states. there are also significant differences in other aspects affecting the extent of protection provided, as well as in operating procedures and financing methods. the lack of harmonisation prevents effective and equal protection of consumers, which may lead to a loss of confidence in the relevant markets and ultimately to a threat to market stability. in addition, it may distort cross-border competition and thus impede the functioning of the internal insurance market. however, the development of harmonised insurance guarantee schemes could contribute to remedying the existing shortcomings. in order to maintain consumer confidence in both the insurance industry and the single market for financial services, in my view a uniform level of consumer protection for all types of insurance products should be ensured. the consumer should have confidence that all types of insurance products purchased are covered by insurance guarantee schemes and that these schemes will guarantee that he will receive, within the prescribed time, a 100% refund that is uniform throughout the european union.

in writing. − the draft regulation aims at implementing article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. it was adopted in may 2001 as a protocol to the un convention against transnational organized crime. it entered into force on 3 july 2005 after being ratified by 40 countries and is the first binding instrument regulating small arms adopted at a global level. the proposed regulation lays down the export procedure to be applied by member states for exports to third countries. its adoption would allow for the application of article 10 of the un protocol in all member states, thereby creating a uniform system for trade in firearms, their parts, components and ammunition within the union. the aim of harmonising and simplifying the procedures applied is complemented by the effort to contribute to the fight against the illicit trade in firearms by promoting and strengthening cooperation between states. it concerns the trade in and transport to third countries of non-automatic firearms, their parts and ammunition for civilian (non-military) purposes, including with regard to countries not party to the un protocol. i believe it is important that article 10 of the un protocol is applied in all member states in order to harmonise procedures in order to establish a common system for regulating the trade in firearms.

the findings of recent studies confirm that, despite the extensive activities and interventions of the european institutions, the business conditions of smes are not improving. most member states only formally assess the quality of the legislative environment for smes and do not even bother to implement european law in this area. in view of the critical economic situation in europe, we should put more pressure on the member states to remove the unnecessary bureaucratic burden. in fact, a small businessman, such as a baker or a restaurant operator, must regularly file various detailed reports with up to six government agencies. for each change in business, it needs to go through new approval and authorisation procedures, thus bypassing at least three or more state offices. but what about those countries whose economic growth we now envy? it's where the small businessman does his business, pays his taxes, and that's it. so let's try to simplify the mechanisms for small businesses.

in writing. the mobility of workers within the european union has long been treated as a potential problem. although the contracts contain the concept of free movement of workers, member states are free to introduce temporary restrictions. the reason is almost always the same: the flow of immigrants from poorer states to richer states, and the citizens of the host state may lose their jobs. but these fears are unfounded. the mobility of workers has a positive impact on the eu as a whole. however, we can say that very few workers are exercising their right to mobility. we need to harmonise national and eu regulations as soon as possible. existing eu strategies need to be adapted to the effects of labour mobility and the increasing role of smes. the involvement of smes is key to this process, as their development guarantees job creation. the importance of information and knowledge is also of paramount importance. in many member states, the current level of information is inadequate. the mobility of workers should be strongly supported and information should be easily accessible to all those concerned. more effort is also needed in educational programs. the coordination of education policies and the acceleration of the recognition of diplomas should be emphasised in order to increase the likelihood of reaching an agreement on how to prepare the active population for changes in the market and the competitive constraints therein.
in writing. the right to move freely for work is one of the most important rights of eu citizens. unfortunately, there are still many problems associated with mobility, which we must try to eliminate for our citizens in order to make this privilege work for them in practice. first of all, cooperation between all the competent authorities and bodies in the individual member states, coordination of their activities and improvement of the quality of control mechanisms and inspection services is important. mobile workers continue to face enormous discrimination and abuse of their rights. we must therefore ensure that they have access to sufficient information on their rights, obligations and options regarding work and residence abroad and that they have adequate legal and social protection. we must try to create legislation that guarantees them the same rights as those at home, including the right to equal pay, the right to strike, to do business under the same conditions, to have a family with them in a foreign country, who also have access to education, health care, etc. i also highly value and support the creation of programmes that promote mobility, such as erasmus and various twinning programmes. mobility within the eu is a great motivator for our citizens even in these times of crisis, and it is up to us to create and secure the best possible conditions for them.
according to the commission's report, nine out of ten jobs are created in the services sector. a functioning single market for services is therefore essential if the european union is to be competitive on the world stage. the european union and its member states are currently in the throes of a major crisis, unemployment is rising and job creation is uncertain. it is therefore necessary that all the single market instruments are fully implemented in all member states, while ensuring that all aspects are functioning, such as the points of the single treaty. the peer review process is a tool that is based on a thorough evaluation of the regulatory framework for services. only such a peer review mechanism will be able to ensure that the single market within the union functions as it should.
the creation of a single market for services has been one of the cornerstones of the european project from its very beginning. the single market in services was not conceived as an end in itself. it is a tool for improving the daily lives and prosperity of european businesses, but also of the citizens of the member states of the union. the huge potential it offers should be used as a lever to create sustainable growth and jobs, to expand consumer choice and to provide new opportunities for businesses. all of this applies in a big way right now in a time of crisis. for example, the peer review process has shown that the member state in which the service is provided often imposes insurance obligations on cross-border service providers. this is regardless of the fact that the provider concerned may already be adequately insured at the place of establishment. this causes considerable problems in the cross-border provision of services in sectors such as business services or construction. i would therefore ask the commission to consider whether such obstacles, which still exist today, cannot be removed for the future, both for the better prosperity of european businesses and for greater efficiency in the provision of services to the citizens of the member states.
thank you, madam president. alternative dispute resolution has become a definite social, legal and economic technique. justice is essential in environmental, labour and international economic relations. in the committee on legal affairs, mrs wallis' report was prepared in the interest of a safer and more efficient eu system. the increasing number of procedures indicates the need to harmonise the legal framework within the union. legal certainty and the protection of consumer rights can be enhanced in a more transparent and coordinated system at european level. it is more important than making alternative dispute resolution mandatory to promote more intensive communication and cooperation between member states and competent professional organisations at union level. adequate information on dispute resolution options for citizens and smes can save significant energy and costs for society and the economy. in addition to the safeguards at member state level, the eu has a role to play in ensuring that 27 states benefit from the benefits of alternative dispute resolution in the single market.
access to justice is a fundamental right. the aim of judicial proceedings, as well as of alternative dispute resolution, is to make such efforts as would lead to the restoration of legal reconciliation or to the resolution of disputes between the parties. alternative dispute resolution helps consumers and traders to resolve conflicts through a third party out-of-court and thus becomes an effective alternative to litigation, in particular in terms of cost. it is regrettable that the knowledge and awareness of citizens of the member states of the union about the very existence of systems and alternative dispute resolution is relatively low. and only a small percentage of citizens know how to submit a complaint to an adr body itself. i therefore believe that it is necessary to promote the public awareness of the potential for dispute resolution also through mechanisms such as alternatives to litigation. they offer the possibility of avoiding a direct confrontational approach while at the same time providing a mutually beneficial solution to the dispute. however, a balanced approach should be sought, taking into account the scope of competence of adr systems on the one hand and fair procedures and treatment of stakeholders on the other.
i support the idea of finding a deal. i consider it useful to harmonise the procedures for alternative dispute resolution in commercial and property disputes in order to increase legal certainty. consumers and businesses alike will certainly appreciate the efforts of the commission and parliament to continuously improve the out-of-court settlement mechanism. it's a win-win situation for both sides. however, i would point out that the family mentioned in the title of the report does not fall within the competence of the union and its institutions. like mrs roith, i consider this a very sensitive issue which requires respect for different national traditions and social conditions. one standard is not enough. recall the problems that have arisen in trying to resolve international divorce at the european level, and consider the lack of representation of the child in the mediation process between the two parents.
alternative dispute resolution in civil, commercial and family matters can in many cases become a quieter, cheaper and faster form of dispute resolution. it is therefore important that the european public is well informed about the relevant legislative frameworks and the possibilities that they offer. in particular, the regulation establishing a european small claims procedure and the directive on certain aspects of mediation in civil and commercial matters provide a common european basis for cross-border and national alternative dispute resolution. i agree that a good level of awareness among the public and businesses of the benefits of adr will help to increase the use of these methods and relieve the courts of the burden of resolving consumer and family disputes in particular. the use of out-of-court family dispute resolution options that reduce the psychological burden on the disputing partners as well as on the children is certainly a better solution than a protracted dispute with evidence and witnesses. it is therefore also appropriate to promote the application of sound alternative dispute resolution at all levels.

in writing. − the proposal aims to codify council directive 92/23/eec of 31 march 1992 on the construction and fitting of tyres for motor vehicles and their trailers. the new directive replaces several acts forming the subject of the codification; the proposal fully preserves the content of the codified acts and limits itself exclusively to consolidating them into a single act, the formal amendments not going beyond the necessary purpose of codification. that directive has been substantially amended several times. i believe that, in the interests of clarity and rationality, it is therefore necessary to codify this directive. it is one of the separate directives of the ec type-approval system established by directive 2007/46/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 5 september 2007 establishing a framework for the type-approval of motor vehicles and their trailers, of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, and laying down the technical prescriptions to be complied with by motor vehicles and their trailers, which relate, inter alia, to tyres. those technical requirements relate to the approximation of the laws of the member states in order to allow the application of the ec type-approval process laid down by the directive in question to each type of motor vehicle and trailer. however, this directive should be without prejudice to the obligations of the member states relating to the time limits for transposition into national law.

in writing. the proposal contains an amendment to the directive on measures against the emission of gaseous and particulate pollutants from engines for use in agricultural or forestry tractors. its objective is to guarantee the free movement of these economic machines while reducing the permitted level of exhaust emissions from engines in order to protect the health and quality of life of citizens and the environment. that directive introduces gradually decreasing limit values for each successive stage in accordance with the different dates set to align with the maximum emission limit values for exhaust gases and particulate matter. as a consequence of the technical studies carried out in 2007, 2009 and 2010 and confirmed by the impact assessment carried out by the commission, it was determined that it is not technically feasible for tractors classified in categories t2, c2 and t4. 1 to meet the requirements of stages iiib and iv within the time limits set. in order to prevent union legislation from laying down technical requirements which cannot be met and thus prevent tractors of that category from being type-approved and placed on the market or put into service, it is necessary to provide for a transitional period of three years during which they may still be type-approved and placed on the market or put into service. directive 2000/25/ec should therefore, in my view, be amended accordingly.
in writing. − the maximum exhaust emissions of carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from diesel engines of non-road mobile machinery are regulated in directive 97/68/ec. the 2004 revision of the directive (2004/26/ec) introduced the current exhaust emission limits for the current stage and set the dates and limit values for the next stage. these stricter limits have been applied since january 2011. machinery covered by this directive includes various types of ground-based machinery, for example, for construction, forestry and agriculture. however, it also applies to locomotives, rolling stock and inland waterway vessels. the 2004 directive also introduced a so-called 'flexible system' which allows manufacturers to place on the market between two successive stages of the exhaust emission limit values a limited number of machines equipped with engines which still comply with the exhaust emission limit values of the previous stage. the limit is set either as 20% of the machines of the total annual sales of the manufacturer, which is calculated as a five-year average of the total sales of the manufacturer, or as a fixed number of machines. the fixed number option is intended for smaller producers. the directive is an important part of the union's environmental legislation, it makes a major contribution to reducing emissions and i believe that its revision should seek to achieve consistency between the relevant requirements and the legislation.
in writing. − the european institutions and the european parliament itself have in the past focused attention on the issue of disabled people on several occasions and have always sought to promote legal standards that guarantee the protection of the rights of disabled people. i believe that even now, long-term investments for the benefit of disabled people should be prioritised, as opposed to short-term one-off expenditure. i personally think it is essential that disabled people (regardless of the severity of their disability) are given assistance that meets their individual needs. at the same time, it is essential to make efforts to create conditions that minimise the need for personalised assistance in a truly barrier-free environment. because even if we talk about integration as integration into society, these people are full members of society. however, integration must be pursued through acceptance. opportunities are equal when the same effort leads to similar results, when there are adequate, defined conditions and means. it is not possible to apply a uniform model to all member states as regards the possibilities of study, employment, free movement and various other activities, as the obstacles faced by disabled people differ from one case to another. however, one aspect should be common: the provision of adequate accommodation and guarantees related to disability, which help to live fully in society.

in writing. − forty years ago, the directive on european law on the coordination of public procurement procedures entered into force. while european public procurement law has contributed to greater transparency in procurement, the fight against corruption, the professionalisation of contracting authorities and the reduction of prices, it is precisely the price reduction that has come at the expense of quality and innovation or the increase in other costs. the commission's efforts to ensure that public procurement law in the member states of the european union is simplified and more flexible through the revision are therefore welcome. however, i believe that it should be done in such a way that the best practices that are in place cannot be called into question. i also believe that our aim should be to reach a compromise on issues such as environmental and social challenges in public procurement policy, the quality of work done, including adequate pay, equality and social cohesion - all in the interests of achieving optimal conditions for citizens, businesses, employees and taxpayers. in relation to the general principle of public procurement, the lowest price should no longer be the decisive factor for the award of contracts. the most economically advantageous offer in terms of the cost of the services or goods concerned should be the decisive one. it is necessary to simplify public procurement law again in such a way as to return to its original essence of guaranteeing transparency, non-discrimination and ensuring competition.
in writing. − a properly functioning eu-wide public procurement market is essential to stimulate competition and innovation in the single market. i support the idea of transnational public procurement. the uniform european public procurement rules make a significant contribution to increasing transparency and equality of treatment, but they need to be further simplified and red tape removed in order to give access to smes. the challenge for member states remains to transpose european rules into national law and to ensure sufficient training, as public procurement requires a high level of professionalism. public procurement must not lead to a reduction in environmental and social standards. i therefore take the view that the criterion of the lowest price should no longer be the determining criterion for the award of contracts and should be replaced by the criterion of the most economically advantageous tender in terms of economic, social and environmental benefits, taking into account the life-cycle costs of the goods, services or works concerned. the report presented sets out the main principles which i believe should guide public procurement in the future and which i am happy to support with my vote.
in writing. − labour migration within the member states of the european union has long been perceived as a potential problem in terms of labour shortages, negatively affecting collective bargaining and wages in the host countries. to strengthen european identity and as a guarantee for the completion of the single market, the free movement of persons is treated contractually. however, member states are entitled to retain, for a transitional period, obstacles to the opening up of the labour market to new member states of the union. however, past fears, notably fears of large immigrant influxes, job losses for host country nationals or declining wages, were never met. on the contrary, there is a clear and obvious added value for the eu as a whole. no jobs were left unfilled, productivity in the member states did not fall and the income of workers who chose to provide their services in another member state increased. i am therefore convinced that it is very important to promote labour mobility and to remove all existing legal, administrative and practical obstacles to the free movement of workers. it is desirable to focus attention as a priority on the establishment of cooperation mechanisms aimed at preventing the negative impacts of mobility, protecting in particular families with children. today, faced with the consequences of the economic and financial crisis, it is more than necessary for member states to support each other, to grow and to progress together.
in writing. − the free movement of workers is one of the fundamental principles of the european union. its aim is to enable nationals of the member states to pursue their profession or to conduct their business in any member state of the european union of their choice, without any obstacles or restrictions. contrary to misconceptions, free movement of workers does not harm national labour markets in terms of reducing wages or increasing unemployment among domestic workers. on the contrary, mobility has a positive impact on productivity growth, which is of paramount importance in times of economic crisis. free movement of workers also creates relatively little direct competition for domestic workers, as they occupy positions in sectors where domestic workers are either not qualified for the job or do not want to do it. the area of labour mobility is a very important issue for the future and a common policy is needed to ensure that it is managed effectively and that it is managed in a way that gradually increases employment, and i therefore fully support this proposal.
in writing. − the mobility of workers is one of the fundamental freedoms underpinning the idea of european integration. in this sense, i support any initiative that facilitates the free movement of workers within the eu for work. however, i do not agree that the european institutions and legislation should intervene in the area of family policy under the pretext of increasing the flexibility of the labour market. the definition of the family and family policy are the exclusive competence of the member states. i regret that the author of this otherwise stimulating report has chosen to go beyond his competence. in article 21, it gives member states its definition of the family, which includes sexual orientation. i cannot therefore, in principle, agree with its attempt to impose on the member states, indirectly, the definition of family and marriage for the various forms of cohabitation.
in writing. − the services directive was adopted in 2006 and remains an important tool for creating a fully functioning single market in services. member states are making significant efforts to implement it. the peer review process is laid down in article 39 of the services directive. this is the first time that this instrument has been used in an eu legal instrument. its main objective within the framework of the directive is to assess the situation in the internal market for services after the introduction of the directive. however, the article remains unclear as far as the precise objectives of peer review are concerned. the result of this lack of precision is that stakeholders and policy makers have different expectations and perceptions of the process. similarly, it is a common mistake to link peer review to the implementation and transposition of the services directive. member states were divided into 6 groups, each with 5 countries, for the peer evaluation activity. the overall assessment of peer review as a policy tool is positive. i am of the opinion that the peer review process should continue to operate in the form of group discussions. however, it is essential to increase the transparency of the process. a certain level of confidentiality is necessary to facilitate discussions between the administrative authorities of the member states, but interested parties should have access to regular reports.
in writing. − if you have the development of the world economy in recent decades has brought growth and prosperity and has lifted millions out of poverty. many others, however, continue to face poverty. social and economic disparities between and within countries must be reduced and europe's fight against poverty must therefore be one of the main priorities of the eu 2020 strategy. the united states and europe are currently still dealing with the consequences of the worst international economic recession since the great depression. the development of the world economy has been marked by imbalances in recent decades, and these are still primarily caused by insufficient competition. given the high degree of globalisation and the scale of capital flows, these imbalances pose new challenges for global governance and challenge the fabric of the current institutional set-up. global imbalances pose a potential threat to financial and macroeconomic stability in dominant economies and have implications for other economies. in my view, it is important that the eu takes a leading role in the reform of the world economy aimed at increasing the legitimacy, transparency and accountability of international institutions, while acting in a unified manner on international economic issues. it is necessary for the union to promote fair trade, democracy, human rights, decent work and sustainable development in its trade policies at all times, in accordance with the treaty of lisbon, its internal programme and the millennium development goals.
in writing. − to recover from the crisis, we must address the inequalities arising from structural imbalances and lack of economic competitiveness. we need to do this in both surplus and deficit countries. it is essential to strengthen and deepen the european single market. however, this should not prevent the european union from making full use of the flexibility provided by the wto to restore the balance of basic macroeconomic factors and to increase prosperity. we also need to reduce our energy dependence so that we can curb imported inflation and restore the balance of trade with oil-producing countries. the commission needs to take a more decisive stance to engage member states and to highlight the positive impact of a stronger economic governance framework for global cooperation and coordination in the eu and the euro area. the financial and economic crisis has repeatedly demonstrated that capital inflows from global imbalances need to be accompanied by responsible monetary policy and strong financial regulation.
in writing. − the negative consequences of the economic and financial crisis, which we are seeing and feeling in all the member states of the european union, are particularly affecting women. single mothers in particular are often overlooked and oversimplified. in many societies, especially those dominated by patriarchal models, the position of the unmarried mother is disregarded. many view single-mother motherhood as a so-called temporary condition that will be resolved as soon as the single mother finds a mate. this distorted view, however, further complicates the position of single mothers in society. it is therefore necessary to respond to this by adjusting the policies. the gravity of the situation has tended to increase in recent times and it is therefore a matter of priority to address this issue and to pay greater attention to the situation of single mothers. i believe that it is desirable for member states to adopt public policies, including education policies, care provision, health policies, employment policies, social security systems and housing policies, which will facilitate the living conditions of single-parent families, especially in view of the reality of single-mother families.

in writing. − organized crime creates significant social costs as it misappropriates resources, disrupts the common free market, damages the transparency of businesses and the legal economy, promotes corruption, pollutes and destroys the environment, violates human rights and undermines democratic principles. it is essential that the institutions of the european union make a concrete political effort with tangible and significant results in the fight against organised crime. of particular importance is the fact that organised crime often takes advantage of globalisation, the removal of borders within the eu and legislative differences between member states to generate ever-greater profits while guaranteeing impunity. criminal groups have built up a network of supporters and sympathizers and have infiltrated the sphere of politics as well as public administration, as is often confirmed by the findings of investigations. the treaty of lisbon opens up new possibilities and new instruments at union level in terms of judicial and police cooperation, as well as in terms of the bodies responsible for combating transnational organised crime and the establishment of common rules aimed at making this fight more effective. it is essential, in particular, to strengthen and improve the functioning of european structures which deal in different ways with the fight against organised crime, and last but not least, in my view, to fully apply the principle of mutual recognition of criminal decisions and to improve judicial cooperation between member states and third countries.
in writing. − the european union is at the forefront of the fight to improve living standards in developing countries. in overseeing the achievement of the millennium development goals, the need for general consistency in joint activities is always advocated. in the fight against poverty, it is crucial to raise as much development finance as possible from all available sources. the union is not only one of the most important donors of official development assistance, but also offers developing countries a comprehensive set of measures to promote sustainable development, in particular by working with partner countries to develop an aid delivery strategy. although oda is one of the best indicators of official donor commitments, it is not the only source of development finance. an increasing share of total oda comes from developing countries that are not members of the oecd. however, regardless of this, transparency and accountability are essential conditions for the effectiveness of aid, not only between the governments of donor and recipient countries, but also between the state and society. the conditions for development aid are constantly changing and the emergence of new donors should be better reflected in the mechanisms to ensure aid effectiveness. i believe it is appropriate that the eu and its member states continue to pay due attention to the quality of aid and to support the international development agenda.

by amending the council directive on the common system of taxation, we could contribute to the taxation of the profits of parent multinational companies which arrive in the parent company's country from subsidiaries from countries which attract capital flows by not properly taxing capital coming from third countries. most often, such profits come from tax havens and are often declared as royalties for the exploitation of intellectual property. such profits then pass through the country of the subsidiary to the parent company established in a member state of the european union, often without any taxation. in this way, multinational companies avoid paying tax on their profits and do not contribute their fair share to the financing of the social needs of their state. a similar mechanism applies to dividends received by parent companies from their subsidiaries in neighbouring switzerland. the solution proposed by mr giegold thus requires that some 25% of the tax be levied in the country of arrival, if it was not previously levied in the country of origin. at a time when our countries' national budgets need every euro, this proposal may seem to be one of the ways to improve the budget.

the proposed revision of the financial regulation for the european union after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon was intended to bring more transparency as well as administrative and financial simplification of the rules. it is of particular importance that the assessment of research funding, for example, be based not only on the type of research but also on whether the research is in line with the fundamental values of the european union, the protection of fundamental human rights and, in particular, the protection of human dignity. such an assessment must also be made in accordance with the recent judgment of the european court of justice in oliver brüstle v greenpeace, which prohibits the patenting of discoveries in areas where the fundamental principles guaranteeing human dignity and integrity are not respected, and in which the court emphasises that the human body at any stage of its formation or development, including embryonic cells, is also covered by such protection.
in writing. the implementation of the financial regulation and the detailed rules for the implementation of the annual budget of the union must comply with the ecj judgment c 34-10. it stated that human life begins at conception and that the human embryo deserves legal protection. the court stated that 'a 'human embryo' is any human ovum from the stage of fertilisation, any unfertilised human ovum in which the nucleus of a mature human cell has been implanted and any unfertilised human ovum which, by means of parthenogenesis, has been induced to divide and develop'. the court pointed out that the community legislature intended to exclude any possibility of patentability where respect for human dignity could be affected. this judgment must be fully applied now to research projects financed by the community budget in progress, and with a view to the programming of the 8th research framework programme. i call on the commission to present a draft framework programme which gives priority to ethical alternatives to basic research. many serious scientific studies have shown that biomedical research is possible without the use of human embryos. europe can be proud of its capacity for competitive scientific research respecting universal ethical foundations.

in writing. − norway is our closest non-eu partner in cooperation on the european gnss systems galileo and egnos. from a political, technological and financial perspective, norway has a long-standing contribution to all phases of the galileo programme through its membership of the european space agency and several years of informal participation in the ec's governance structures in relation to the galileo programme. the agreement formalising cooperation between norway and the european union in the field of satellite navigation also lays down the general principles of cooperation and the rights and obligations of norway in those areas, in particular as regards security, which are not covered by the existing acquis relating to galileo. the agreement is necessary because two important ground installations will be installed in norway and will contribute to the proper functioning of the system. in this context, norway undertakes a political commitment to contribute to the future union policy on the protection of european gnss systems. the commission negotiated the agreement with the kingdom of norway and it was subsequently signed on 22 september 2010. however, it is also necessary for all member states to ratify it. it is appropriate to apply the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on a provisional basis pending its entry into force.
in writing. − the agreement on the promotion, provision and use of the galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and associated applications between the united states of america, on the one hand, and the european community and its member states, on the other, was signed at dromoland castle in ireland on 26 june 2004 and is applied provisionally from 1 november 2008 until its entry into force. the united states currently provides the standard gps positioning service for peaceful civilian, commercial and scientific use on a continuous, worldwide basis, without direct user charges, and the european community is developing and planning to operate the civilian global satellite navigation, timing and positioning system galileo. provided that these two systems are radio frequency compatible and interoperable at user level, they could increase the number of satellites visible from any location on earth and improve the accessibility of navigation signals by civilian users worldwide. and it is precisely the aim of this agreement to provide a framework for cooperation between interested parties in the promotion, provision and use of signals and navigation and time management services. in the light of the commission's proposal and the consent of the european parliament, i consider that an agreement should be concluded.
in writing. - colleagues, the galileo navigation system is a satellite system which should become an alternative to the american gps and the russian glonass systems. both are competitive and, unlike galileo, funded by the military branches of these countries. this system should be operational from 2014. galileo has many advantages, including, for example, full civilian funding or full compatibility with the us and russian navigation systems. the first two satellites were launched last week and we were able to watch the launch live at the ep's brussels headquarters. unfortunately, this launch was not without its complications and had to be moved. the european union started the first negotiations on the introduction of this system as early as 1999. there are now voices that question whether we will be able to meet the planned date in 2014 when the system should be operational (but only in test mode). i personally have high hopes that the european space agency will be able to launch the planned 18 satellites needed to put the system into test operation. we all know that the european union is lagging behind its us counterparts in areas such as development and research, and it is the successful implementation of a system such as galileo that will reduce the competitive edge.

for the efd group. the discovery of antimicrobials in the last century was one of the most important milestones in the history of medicine. mankind found a weapon against enemies who had previously recklessly slaughtered human lives, often in devastating epidemics. today, however, the proportion of microorganisms that are resistant to these drugs is beginning to grow dangerously. efforts to save and preserve the lineage of microorganisms force them to adapt to the drug used, or they die. those bacteria that learn to survive in the presence of antibiotics continue to grow, mutate, multiply, and complicate treatment and sometimes death. they're spread from hospitals to other people. unfortunately, we're not finding any new active ingredients. only 1.6% of the medicines currently in development are antibiotics. so from this perspective, we can say with some degree of certainty that we are in the process of total antibacterial disarmament. the world health organization has therefore proposed a set of measures to stop the spread of drug resistance. experts have identified other factors that, in addition to the misuse of antimicrobials, promote resistance. in particular, they pointed to the incomplete national rules on the use of these medicines and their lack of binding effect. the 2001 council recommendation on the prudent use of antimicrobials in human medicine also appears to be insufficient from the point of view of practical application. so i would like to remind you of the world health organization's motto for this year's world health day, the fight against antimicrobial resistance, which is: no action today, no treatment tomorrow.

for the s&d group. the socialist and democratic group sees the commission's proposal to revise the original 2004 directive as part of the effort to establish a common european asylum policy by 2012. in the case of the original directive, the european parliament had only consultative powers. now, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament has the possibility of co-decision. the existing directive includes two key elements. first, the grounds on which the person concerned is entitled to refugee status or subsidiary protection and, second, the content of that protection in terms of the rights of residence and employment, but also the social rights, in the member state responsible for protection. the main change proposed is to bring these two categories of protection much closer together. the main objective is, on the one hand, to ensure that member states apply common criteria for the identification of persons genuinely in need of international protection. on the other hand, the directive should ensure that some minimum level of benefits is available to those persons in all member states. in order to make the benefits and rights provided more effective, it is essential to take into account the specific needs and particular problems faced by beneficiaries of international protection in their integration. the problem of financial constraints also needs to be addressed. it in its way limits their access to employment-related education and training opportunities and thus deprives them of being a truly integral part of our democratic society. in conclusion, commissioner, i wish you every success and do not be discouraged by the cries of various populists who are against both asylum and immigration policy. we're holding your hand.

the proposed amendments to the international protection directive aim to reduce the current disparities in the recognition of refugee status between the member states of the union. different internal policies and perceptions of union policy in the member states, as well as different experiences of national institutions with the adaptation and integration of asylum seekers in their countries, lead member states to seek to implement the current directive as they see fit in their experience. i therefore understand that up to six informal trialogue sessions were required to prepare the material submitted. the commission's attempt to interfere with the best practices of the national institutions under the pretext of a greater unification of the asylum system may rightly be met with disagreement, particularly among experienced officials, when certain terms are defined in a manner which is fundamentally different from that which has been used up to now. i therefore believe that the updating of the directive should be carried out in a pragmatic and sensitive manner and with full respect for the views of the experienced national institutions which are implementing our asylum policy in practice. only then can we succeed in our process.

in writing. − the european ombudsman, nikiforos diamandouros, was re-elected by the european parliament in its plenary session on 20 january 2010 in strasbourg and was sworn in before the court of justice of the european union on 25 october 2010 in luxembourg. in may of that year, he presented the 2010 annual report to the president of the european parliament, jerzy buzek. where possible, the ombudsman tries to achieve a positive outcome by seeking a friendly solution that satisfies both the complainant and the institution. in 2010, 179 cases were settled amicably. however, if an acceptable solution cannot be found, the case is either closed with a critical remark or a draft recommendation is drawn up. the 2010 annual report pays particular attention to the new strategy defined by the ombudsman and his staff for the 2009-2014 term of office. it is mainly about broadening and deepening contacts with the eu institutions and civil society, working to resolve complaints more quickly, and providing useful information to stakeholders and the public. the ombudsman will use this new strategy to consolidate and manage his work to ensure that eu citizens can fully enjoy their rights and thus improve the quality of the union's administration.
