in writing. − the european legal framework allowing airlines to transfer passenger name record data was established by council decision 2008/651/cfsp/jha of 30 june 2008 by signing the agreement between the european union and australia on the processing and transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data originating in the union, by air carriers, to the australian customs and border protection agency. since june 2008, the agreement has been applied provisionally, but only in seventeen eu member states, as no unanimous agreement was reached on its conclusion. on 15 february 2010, the council requested the european parliament to give its consent to a new pnr agreement with australia. it subsequently adopted a resolution in may 2010 in which it decided to postpone the vote on this consent request, delaying the conclusion of the agreement and leading to the opening of new negotiations between the commission and australia in january 2011. the clear purpose of this agreement is to establish the conditions under which passenger name record data may be transferred and used and the way in which it is protected. however, there is legal uncertainty as to whether the draft agreement complies with european union data protection legislation and is therefore compatible with the treaties in this respect. the european parliament therefore requests the court of justice to give an opinion on the compatibility of the agreement in question with the treaties.
in writing. − australian legislation empowers the australian customs service to require any air carrier operating passenger flights to and from australia to provide it with electronic access to passenger name record (pnr) data prior to their arrival in or departure from australia. the purpose of such a procedure is to obtain pnr data in electronic form prior to arrival, thereby enabling the australian customs to carry out an effective and efficient risk assessment of the passenger and facilitating travel. such steps can enhance australia's security and, in line with the policy to combat terrorism and other serious crime, will also strengthen international police and judicial cooperation between australia and europe. the european parliament initially decided in may 2010 to postpone the vote on the consent to the said agreement, but later welcomed the discussion of a new agreement, setting out its criteria for giving consent to the conclusion of agreements with third countries on the transfer of pnr data. it has examined the new draft eu-australia pnr agreement and has concluded that many of the required criteria have been sufficiently met and therefore gives its consent to the conclusion of the agreement.

in writing. − antimicrobials are substances that are able to completely destroy bacteria, viruses and other microorganisms, or at least prevent them from multiplying and growing. they therefore play an important role in improving public health by helping to reduce deaths from diseases or infections that were previously incurable or fatal. however, as a result of the use of antimicrobials, some microorganisms that were originally sensitive to these substances have developed so-called antimicrobial resistance. in humans, this is often caused primarily by incorrect treatment or inadequate dosage of antibiotic-containing medicines. it is a serious public health problem in europe and worldwide, and as a result, treatment becomes longer and more complex. the quality of life is greatly reduced, the risk of death increases, and so do the costs of health care. i therefore believe that it is essential to take immediate action to prevent or reverse the further increase in the number of resistant microorganisms. however, patients should be cautious when using available antibiotics, and should strictly adhere to dosage, duration of treatment, and the possibility of combining them with other medicines. it is essential to raise awareness in the member states of the public health risks posed by antimicrobial resistance and to promote, through adequate measures, a more responsible use of antibiotics as such.
the number and frequency of self-immolations by nuns and monks in tibet is increasing alarmingly. as someone who grew up under the communist dictatorship, it is clear to me that the main reason for these tragedies is the atmosphere of fear, of unfreedom created and maintained by the chinese communist regime. as one of the world's oldest cultures, tibet certainly deserves more respect, freedom and independence than it is currently receiving from the rulers in beijing. the european union and the european parliament must continue to put pressure on china to open bilateral negotiations with tibetan officials, led by the dalai lama. even a hint of such a move would greatly reduce tensions and bring hope to all tibetans. the benefits of such a decision would be felt immediately throughout the tibet region, and the tragic self-immolation would become history.

despite considerable support from the european union, rail transport is stagnating and still lagging behind road transport. the first railway package of 2001 did not meet expectations of a significant improvement and attractiveness of the railway sector. the persisting differences in national rules mean that, while air or road transport crosses borders without obstacles, the international rail service faces technical and legislative obstacles when crossing borders. therefore, if we are to continue to build a common integrated railway area we need to harmonise more closely the rules governing transport on the union's rail network. only by simplifying road transport can we increase the competitiveness of rail transport compared to road or air transport. the organisational separation of the railway infrastructure network from the transport and service operators will certainly help to make the competitive environment in the railway sector more attractive. however, it is also necessary to have in mind the precise allocation of responsibilities, in particular for security, between the various actors involved in the operation of the whole system. rail transport is considered safe, but rail accidents usually cause great damage. it is therefore necessary to collect data on these accidents at european union level.

the online gambling sector is growing alongside the increasing spread of mobile and internet communication technologies. while member states are free to regulate their own environment to a certain extent, this must be in line with european internal market legislation. however, gambling operators from other countries with open markets and low tax rates are also available in countries where online gambling is prohibited. there is also an unregulated black market on the internet. internet gambling is also widely available to minors or to people prone to compulsive gambling. we should therefore jointly seek the appropriate framework for the responsible regulation of this environment. the european court of justice has already ruled that gambling is not a regular service and that its regulation in accordance with appropriately defined objectives is permissible. it would therefore be appropriate to define minimum standards for consumer protection in the area of online gambling in order to allow for a more stringent prosecution of such activities in the member states.
in writing. beekeeping is a traditional rural activity that often provides a secondary income for rural households. in central europe, the biodiversity of the flora is relatively well preserved, which makes it possible to produce high-quality flower and honey honey without major investment. under these conditions, the area is able to supply honey as a genuine natural product suitable for the consumption of the population. prices are of course higher than in some parts of the world outside europe, but they also provide a supplementary source of food for the population, with a higher and cleaner quality. too much openness to products from other countries could result in beekeepers being unable to compete with the pressure of cheap but often not quite high quality honey from professionally run bee farms outside europe, where the use of antibiotics is allowed. failure to maintain domestic bee lines risks their replacement by lines or species that cannot be accepted in densely populated countries, with negative consequences for biodiversity and consequently for bee health. such a situation could seriously damage the interests of our beekeepers. central europe has all the prerequisites to produce high-quality honey as a natural product. it may cover any additional quantitative needs with imports from other parts of the world under clearly defined conditions and labelled for the domestic consumer.

as several decisions and provisions governing the union's state aid rules for services of general economic interest expire at the end of this year, it will be necessary to revise those rules. experience with the application of the current rules tells us that the administrative burden resulting from their application has been excessive and disproportionate, especially for small local authorities, and that several key terms have created misunderstandings and legal uncertainty. therefore, when revising the rules, we must strive to make the new legal instruments simpler, clearer and more understandable. they must be adapted to the environment in which they will be applied so that they can be used in the environment of small local authorities as effectively and efficiently as in more complex cases. only in this way can we contribute to a greater expansion of the necessary services of general economic interest throughout the european union.

in writing. − accession to the athens convention on the carriage of passengers and their luggage by sea is an issue to which the european union and the european parliament itself have devoted attention for some time. the convention was concluded back in 1974 and focused on the safety of passenger ships and the rights of passengers. however, it was considered to be insufficient and it is therefore desirable to incorporate in its content amendments concerning, in particular, the liability of the carrier, compulsory insurance, limitation of liability for death and personal injury, loss of or damage to luggage and vehicles. by means of a protocol adopted on 1 november 2002, the athens convention was amended to cover these key elements. taking into account that the most pressing issues were already covered by the protocol, the commission proposed in 2003 that the eu, together with the member states, become parties to the protocol. the union now has exclusive competence to accede to the protocol to the athens convention as regards the matters covered by that regulation, and other aspects of the protocol not covered by the regulation fall within the competence of the member states. in the light of the procedure applicable to international agreements, accession to the protocol is submitted to parliament for assent and i believe that it is equally appropriate for the committee on transport and tourism to deliver a favourable opinion on the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. − air services between the european union and jordan are currently operated under bilateral agreements between individual member states and jordan. the european commission is now proposing a much more ambitious agreement to replace the bilateral set of agreements by creating a euro-mediterranean airspace between the union and jordan. the agreement establishes uniform conditions for air carriers in all 27 member states and should benefit them irrespective of their nationality. the commission notes that the agreement between the eu and jordan on the air carrier aoc was signed on 27 june 2015 and entered into force on 1 january 2015. the objective of that agreement is to progressively open up markets, to establish non-discriminatory and equal conditions for economic operators on the basis of the eu treaties and to bring jordanian aviation legislation into line with eu legislation as regards safety, security and air traffic management. as the agreement covers not only areas falling within the eu's competence but also areas falling within the competence of the member states, its conclusion requires ratification at eu level as well as in the parliaments of the member states. i am convinced that the conclusion of the euro-mediterranean air transport agreement with jordan is in the interest of the citizens and businesses of the union and in line with the european neighbourhood policy. for this reason too, it is justified for the european parliament to give its consent to its conclusion.

in writing. − differences in the insolvency laws of the member states give companies with crossborder activities competitive advantages and disadvantages and difficulties that could become obstacles to the successful restructuring of insolvent companies. even though it is not possible to establish a body of substantive bankruptcy law at european union level, there are certain areas of insolvency law where harmonisation can be achieved. bankruptcy law should be a tool for rescuing undertakings at union level and, wherever such rescue is possible, it is to the benefit of the debtor, creditors and employees. at the same time, i believe that it is desirable to create a legal framework that is more suited to the situation of temporary insolvency of companies. however, in each individual case, it is necessary to examine the reasons for the insolvency of the undertaking and to determine whether it is merely a case of temporary financial difficulties or of complete insolvency. similarly, the interconnection of national insolvency registers and the subsequent creation of a universally accessible and comprehensive eu insolvency database would allow creditors, shareholders, employees and courts to ascertain whether insolvency proceedings have been opened in another member state, as well as the dates and details of the lodging of claims. such steps would promote a cost-effective administration and increase transparency while respecting data protection.
in writing. − the european union has the oldest population in the world, and tackling demographic change is one of the key challenges for the future. demographic change affects regions differently, and this is driven by a number of factors. the appropriate response to this challenge requires different adaptation strategies. for example, it is clear that the quality of life in regions with a declining population especially in rural areas is defined differently than in regions with an increasing population. however, i believe that in finding the optimal solution, it is essential to take into account the individual needs of different population groups in all circumstances. in order to respond to the challenges of demographic change, it is also important to seek to create conditions that enable the reconciliation of the working, family and private lives of the citizens of the member states of the european union. it is also important to improve coordination between the responsible authorities at all levels so that positive progress can be made, for example through the exchange of experience and good practice on the issue. if we make the necessary efforts to address demographic change appropriately and find answers at european, national and regional levels, europe will not be a threat but an opportunity.
in writing. − europe's population is ageing rapidly, with the longest life expectancy and the lowest population growth rate in the world. the birth rate per woman remains below the survival rate of 2.1 children, while life expectancy is increasing. demographic change is posing new challenges for many regions of the european union. the european commission's communication on promoting solidarity between regions states that the rights of all generations must be guaranteed. the diversity of challenges requires that regions and cities develop their own strategies. this is a fundamental competence of the member states, so it is clear that the regions need to be proactive and to do so they need guidance and perspectives. in the 2007-13 funding period, member states allocated almost eur 30 billion (i.e. 8,5% of the structural funds) to this type of measure in their operational programmes. regional policy is thus a key tool for tackling demographic change. in future, the structural funds should be better adapted to the challenges of demographic change and should be recognised as a horizontal priority in their operational programmes. demographic indicators shall also be taken into account in the regional distribution of structural assistance. i find the expert opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs particularly useful.

in writing. − point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management allows the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) via the flexibility instrument with an annual ceiling of eur 500 million over and above the relevant headings of the financial framework. appropriate legislative and budgetary instruments have been put in place by the european union to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade and to assist them in their reintegration into the labour market. in june 2010, ireland submitted an application egf/2010/20 ie/construction 43 for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in 1 560 enterprises (3 382 redundancies, of which 2 228 are eligible for aid) operating in division 43 specialised construction nace revision 2 in the irish regions border, midlands and western (ie01) and southern and eastern (ie02) at nuts ii level. the application submitted is one of three applications concerning the construction sector in ireland. and since after a thorough examination the commission has come to the conclusion that all the conditions laid down for granting the financial assistance have been duly fulfilled, it is justified to grant the request.
in writing. − the european union has put in place appropriate legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers who are feeling the effects of major structural changes in the world trade pattern and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) has been extended for applications submitted from 1 may 2009 to include support for workers made redundant as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis. point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management allows the egf to be mobilised through the flexibility instrument with an annual ceiling of eur 500 million over and above the corresponding headings of the financial framework. on 3 january 2011, austria submitted an application egf/2011/001 at/niederösterreich-oberösterreich for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in 706 enterprises in the nace revision 2 division 49 road and pipeline transport in the austrian regions of lower austria (niederösterreich) (at12) and upper austria (oberösterreich) (at31) at nuts ii level. after a thorough examination of the application, the commission has concluded that all the conditions laid down for granting the financial contribution have been met and that it is therefore in accordance with the relevant regulation to grant a financial contribution to austria.

in writing. − the joint parliamentary assembly met twice in 2010. the 19th meeting was held in tenerife from 6 to 9 april. in addition to the reports of the standing committees, the meeting adopted resolutions on post-disaster reconstruction in haiti and on the situation in south sudan. six sets of conclusions on regional strategy papers were also adopted for the six acp regions. the 20th meeting was held in kinshasa from 30 november to 3 december. the assembly adopted three resolutions included in the reports of the standing committees and two urgent resolutions on food security and the situation in the sahel-saharan region and a declaration on the results of the presidential elections in côte d'ivoire. during the year, there was also one regional meeting on mahé. after 2009, when no joint parliamentary assembly fact-finding missions were organised, the acp secretariat was again able to finance the costs of three missions in 2010: madagascar, burundi and haiti. the joint parliamentary assembly has become a key player in the field of north-south cooperation through its high-quality work. the european commission is currently submitting country and regional strategy documents to the european parliament and the national parliaments of the acp countries for parliamentary scrutiny. it is important that the development committee and the psc monitor the situation and ensure the effective application of this instrument of parliamentary control.
in writing. − on 9 march 2010, the commission presented a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european union initiative to promote the european heritage label. the proposal aims in particular to strengthen the sense of belonging of european citizens to the eu on the basis of common elements of history and heritage. particular attention is paid to the added value of the brand, which does not, however, speak of the beauty of the site or the quality of its architecture, but rather of the symbolic value for european integration and the history of the union. it is not about protecting the sites as such, but rather about the activities they can offer and their educational and training dimension, especially for young people. the proposal extends an intergovernmental initiative that started back in 2006. it responds to the conclusions adopted by the council in november 2008, which invited the commission to submit a proposal to transform this initiative into a formal union action. parliament's legislative resolution, which was adopted by a large majority at first reading, was accompanied by 62 amendments, most of which concerned matters of relatively minor importance and contributed to further improving the text. consequently, the first reading in the council is based on the agreement negotiated after the first reading in parliament. i consider it appropriate that the council's position at first reading be adopted without amendments and without further delay.
in writing. − during the debate on this decision, the french senate raised the issue of a breach of the principle of subsidiarity. national parliaments must always remain vigilant during the legislative process. there are already two similar tools: the unesco world heritage list and the council of europe's european cultural itineraries. do we really need another one? the 'european heritage' label aims to draw attention to sites or monuments and their symbolism for europe. emphasis shall be placed on promotion, as well as on presenting more detailed explanations of their european dimension and on the organisation of educational activities for young people. it is time to re-emphasise the importance of religious heritage in shaping european consciousness. the label is primarily a tool for promoting national awareness through local heritage or it also speaks of the european significance of the object. to get rid of the official denial of christian roots, sacred sites and monuments should also be marked. whether it's the vendée or the spišské podhradie, monasteries, temples, towers and cemeteries, all of these shape the minds of people and shape the landscape. at the same time, it preserves the values, ideals and symbols of the nations that possess them.
in writing. − if you have with the increasing popularity of road and air transport, rail is becoming less and less preferred. in an effort to remedy the situation, the european union has adopted a number of legislative measures aimed at reviving interest in railways by gradually creating a so-called single european railway area. in the past, it has presented a number of packages and directives, declaring its intention to reform the regulatory framework, to ensure the integration of the rail transport sector at european level and thus to enable it to face competition from other modes of transport. the eu's transport policy has set itself the objective of building an internal market, notably by developing common policies, in an effort to achieve competitiveness also in the field of transport. the draft revised version of the first railway package can make a significant contribution to this objective, also by facilitating the integration and development of the european rail market. in my view, efforts should be made to build a comprehensive and integrated european railway area. the common interests of the eu as a whole - as far as the railway sector is concerned - should take precedence over the interests of the individual member states. a genuine european railway area must be built, in which passengers and goods can be transported without any effort. last but not least, compliance with safety requirements should also be taken into account and this should play an important role in the licensing of railway undertakings.
in writing. − the overwhelming scientific evidence points to climate change, and therefore action is needed to help tackle this major challenge of the 21st century effectively. a broader and more effective european climate diplomacy is needed by all eu institutions ahead of the durban conference, which should aim to present a clearer eu climate policy profile, bringing new momentum to international climate negotiations and encouraging the introduction of binding emission reductions and adequate climate mitigation and adaptation measures. in my view, it would be beneficial for the eu to take the lead and push for an ambitious climate policy, thereby encouraging other countries to follow suit in doing so. at the same time, members of civil society, including representatives of gender equality organisations, should be given the opportunity to actively participate in the activities of the green climate fund management board and all its subsidiary boards. adaptation efforts should systematically and effectively address the impacts of climate change in terms of gender equality in energy, water, food security, agriculture and fisheries, biodiversity and ecosystem services, health, industry, human settlements, disaster management and conflict and security.
in writing. − climate change is one of the biggest environmental, social and economic challenges. despite various conspiracy theories, the warming of the climate system is a confirmed fact. global warming is causing the air and oceans to warm, accelerating the melting of snow and ice, and raising the global average water level. as with the economy and the global financial crisis, it is clear that we are all on the same page when it comes to climate change, because whatever the states decide to do, the consequences will be felt around the world. one of the key debates on creating an effective system of global rules will take place at the end of november in durban, south africa. the need, or rather the necessity, to keep the global average temperature rise below two degrees celsius is one of the european union's top priorities in environmental matters. unfortunately, the failure of a new climate treaty based on the kyoto protocol and its replacement by a voluntary and non-binding framework will simply not be enough to reach the limit of a temperature rise of below 2 degrees. durban needs to send a clear signal and thus a legally binding process to address this problem, because there is no other alternative.
in writing. − the european union member states promised in 2005 to devote 50% of all new aid to sub-saharan africa, but in reality they have only allocated half of this amount and have failed to meet their commitment to allocate 0.15% of gross national income to the least developed countries by 2010. the failure to deliver on aid pledges will seriously undermine confidence in the eu and damage its own credibility as well as that of its partners in the developing world. it is evident that the pressure on national budgets is increasing as a result of the financial and economic crisis. at the same time, i believe that achieving the goal of poverty eradication will require, first and foremost, a change of policy in both industrialised and developing countries to address the structural causes of poverty. the mobilisation of domestic resources in partner countries is key to sustainable development. it is important that european aid providers step up their global efforts to promote tax transparency. the fight against tax havens, tax evasion and illicit capital flight should be a priority in development policy. at the same time, eu policies such as agriculture, fisheries, migration or security must, under the lisbon treaty, be consistent with the eu's development policy objectives and it is desirable to apply policy coherence in the field of development so as to address the structural problem of poverty eradication.
in writing. − culture is at the heart of european identities and common values. it is at the heart of current debates on identity, social cohesion and the development of the knowledge economy. the european audiovisual sector, including cinema, is an important part of the eu economy and should strive to increase its competitiveness. european cinema is an important part of culture, promotes dialogue and understanding, embodies and captures european values in the eu and beyond, and plays an important role in preserving and promoting cultural and linguistic diversity. the digital age offers new opportunities for the sector, in particular in terms of more efficient distribution, screening and accessibility of films and higher quality audio and video. at the same time, however, the digital transition also poses a number of challenges and burdens, particularly in the financial area. the commission notes that the costs of digitisation are not directly linked to the costs of the digital cinema, but are linked to the costs of the digital cinema. it would therefore be appropriate for the commission to propose specific support measures for them. in addition to economic dynamism, european cinema is an important factor in the cultural development and identity of europe. i believe that we should make every effort to preserve the richness of european cinema and to ensure that it is as widely available as possible to citizens, in the interests of unity and freedom of thought.

the essence of net neutrality and the fundamental issues of the debate relate in particular to how best to keep this platform open and ensure that it can continue to provide high-quality services for all and enable the dissemination of innovation. network neutrality affects the whole range of rights and principles enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, in particular with regard to privacy and family life, the protection of personal data and freedom of expression and information. therefore, any legislative proposal in this area will be subject to an in-depth impact assessment on the basis of law and compliance with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. in the absence of net neutrality, there would be serious risks in the form of, for example, anti-competitive behaviour, blocking of innovation, restrictions on freedom of expression and media pluralism, as well as lack of consumer awareness and privacy. this would be detrimental to businesses, consumers and democratic society as a whole.

for the efd group. earlier this year, the commission presented the first eu strategy to integrate roma into mainstream society. the commission wants to solve a problem that has eluded several member states for generations in less than nine years. i do not want to comment on the professional level of the european union framework for national roma integration strategies, but rather to help our officials in the commission understand the problem they are tackling. at the konstantin filozof university in nitra, slovakia, university teachers and staff of the roma culture department have been working on various methods of helping the roma ethnic group for more than twenty years. they prepare and train roma teachers for primary schools as well as specialised social workers for work in roma settlements. i am convinced that the experience of the experts from this unique centre in europe, who have been working with the roma community for more than fifty years, could be very useful for our officials in designing roma strategies.
policy proposals aimed at improving roma inclusion in majority society are fundamentally flawed. they assume that there are some specific roma problems that need to be addressed. but these are not the problems of the roma, but of all the families living on the edge of extreme poverty. these families have trouble finding housing, employment, and regular meals. they have limited access to education, health care, and justice. they have social acceptance issues. and eventually, they give up on trying to get out of a difficult situation on their own. none of these problems will be solved by dividing the people concerned into groups and dealing with each one separately. by talking only about roma, we ignore the facts. the fact is that many roma have succeeded in their professional lives, are respected in their communities, and are responsible parents. it is also a fact that many non-roma are homeless and marginalized or long-term abusers of social systems. if we want every citizen of the european union to have equal access to fundamental rights, we must base our approach on social status, not ethnicity. the so-called roma inclusion will only be achieved if we eliminate extreme poverty and its manifestations.
i know the situation of roma in slovakia very well, because in eastern slovakia, where i live, there are the most roma. i agree with those who say that discrimination against roma exists. but we also have to say that oftentimes, they feel that they are being discriminated against because of it. they're the ones who are responsible for not being adaptable, for not educating their children, for not providing health care, and so on. at the same time, we must say that not all roma are satisfied with their lives - they want to live better, they want to work and they want a better future for their children. last week i visited a settlement in the town of moldava nad bodvou, where four families had their huts burned down in august. thanks to the city's help, which leased the land to them, and a nonprofit organization, the roma themselves are building their future brick dwellings out of recycled building materials. i have documented the efforts of these particular roma families in a short document that shows that roma people want a better life, but they cannot help themselves. so if we want to solve the roma problem, we have to solve it with the roma.
while i do not consider it a sensible and systemic solution to provide reduced vat rates for certain goods and services, i respect the fact that several governments use tax breaks to stimulate selected activities or products. thus, if a country benefits from a reduced rate of value added tax on books, such a reduced rate can also be accepted for their electronic versions. unlike my colleague, mrs gall, i do not see the main purpose of the favours as being their cultural content, but rather their educational content. when we look at the number of textbooks, workbooks and compulsory and recommended literature that our children and young people will pass through in preparation for life, i am convinced that electronic versions of textbooks and work materials, which are now standard in affordable and quality reading devices, can make our pupils and students' school bags much lighter. perhaps this is why such a reduced rate could make sense.
for the efd group. the european atomic energy community framework programme for nuclear research and training follows on from the nuclear research and development measures implemented under the 7th framework programme of the european atomic energy community for 2007 2011. in line with the current financial perspective and time horizon of the 7th framework programme, the proposals cover only the two-year period up to 2013, but are designed in line with the europe 2020 and energy 2020 objectives. although the fukushima nuclear power plant destroyed by a massive tsunami has sparked serious debate about the continued use of nuclear power plants and several union countries have decided to limit or end their use, nuclear research remains an important part of the community's innovation policy. in particular, research into nuclear fission is bringing new insights and more efficient and secure access to a stable carbon-free energy source. the new technologies of the fourth generation of fast neutron reactor systems are up to 50 times more efficient than current systems and will last for thousands of years using currently known and available uranium resources. the european union therefore feels, as does the united states, russia and china, the need to continue nuclear research, both in the field of fission and in the field of fusion. the international thermonuclear experimental reactor, with its accompanying research and development programmes, remains the most important bearer of the perspective of the significant potential of safe, ecological, sustainable and economically accessible energy sources for europe. the new rules for carrying out this research will therefore allow us to continue it at least until 2013.

in writing. − since its creation on 1 july 2002, the international criminal court (icc) has successfully implemented a unique global mandate to prosecute perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. however, despite his efforts, professionalism and determination, he is now at a critical point in his political and financial situation. he is increasingly subject to unjust, politically motivated attacks, his arrest warrants are often not respected, and his current budget does not cover his needs. the european union is a staunch supporter of the icc supporting it from its inception through various political, diplomatic, financial and logistical activities, while helping to promote the universal validity and integrity of the rome statute, contributing to its independence and effective functioning. it is our endeavour and one of our priorities to help the court to tackle the challenging tasks and overcome the political and financial difficulties it currently faces. freedom, the rule of law and the fight against impunity are pillars of sustainable peace, as they guarantee respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. i believe that justice must be seen as an indispensable element in support of efforts to maintain peace and resolve conflicts. in this case, full and prompt cooperation between the parties concerned, including the eu member states and the court, is crucial to the effectiveness and success of the international criminal justice system.

in writing. − many global challenges in the fields of foreign policy, security, development and the environment require common action and transatlantic cooperation, but the economic crisis has now come to the fore, making it one of the main challenges to be addressed today. despite remaining the world's largest economies, the eu and the us are facing major challenges arising from the financial crisis and increasing competition from emerging economies. in my view, there is a need to establish and contribute to the effective functioning of a joint transatlantic initiative to create jobs and growth, including a trade and investment promotion plan. it would be appropriate for the eu and the us to further develop existing cooperation mechanisms, to work towards intensifying joint work on regulatory dialogue, the elimination of tariffs, the removal of unjustified non-tariff barriers and the establishment of common standards that would remove technical barriers to free and fair trade. lastly, the need to ensure freedom and security in one's own country must not result in abandoning basic principles relating to civil liberties and the promotion of common human rights standards. for this reason, and in the spirit of joint efforts to combat the crisis, the need for closer cooperation between europe and the us has perhaps never been more appropriate and necessary.
in writing. − the open nature of the internet is a key driver of competition, economic growth, social development and innovation, which has led to a huge development in online applications, content and services, and thus to growth in the supply and demand for content and services. this openness makes the internet an important engine for the free circulation of knowledge, ideas and information, even in countries where access to independent media is restricted. internet services are offered on a cross-border scale and the internet is at the core of the global economy and as stated in the digital agenda for europe broadband and the internet are important drivers of economic growth, job creation and european competitiveness at global level. i believe that only by stimulating a properly functioning digital internal market will europe be able to fully exploit the potential of the digital economy. each of the proposed solutions to the problem of net neutrality can only be effective through a consistent european approach. it is therefore necessary to closely monitor the adoption of national rules on net neutrality, taking into account their impact on individual national markets as well as on the internal market. because only through cooperation and coordination between member states, in particular between national regulatory authorities, and also cooperation and coordination with the commission, will the union be able to exploit the full potential of the internet.
in writing. − net neutrality and the internet in the european union are very important. this type of neutrality is a position whereby internet and internet service providers or governments themselves may not impose any restrictions on the consumer. the commission, in cooperation with the member states and the european regulatory authority for electronic communications, faces the difficult task of adopting a common approach to the issue of an open internet and neutrality across the eu, as only such a common approach can be truly successful. consumers must be free to choose the type of service they use and from which operator. telecommunications companies must therefore provide clear, meaningful and comparable information to their customers. these measures and the subsequent eu-wide coordination are necessary in particular to avoid potential discriminatory behaviour by operators, such as excessive pricing for voice over internet protocol or sharing of data using file transfer protocol or peer-to-peer. such behaviour not only restricts end-users but also harms competition.
in writing. − if you have on 1 august 2010, the convention on cluster munitions (ccm) and the related role of the european union entered into force. the dkm prohibits the use, production, storage and transport of cluster munitions as a whole category of weapons and requires states parties to destroy stockpiles of such munitions. through that convention, significant and fundamental changes are being made compared to the previous period when cluster munitions were considered a necessity to guarantee military security. twenty-two member states have signed and fifteen have ratified the dkm. however, five member states have not yet taken any of these steps. in my view, it is essential that member states make efforts to implement the convention, to dispose of ammunition stockpiles, to provide the necessary assistance to victims and to assist other states in their efforts to implement the jcpoa in various ways. last but not least, i consider it extremely positive that the convention on cluster munitions states that member states of the european union may never, under any circumstances, use, develop, produce, otherwise acquire, stockpile, preserve or transfer, directly or indirectly, cluster munitions to anyone else.
in writing. − the european union's digital single market is highly fragmented, partly due to the union's tax system, especially with regard to excise duties on goods and services. the economic crisis is seriously damaging and negatively affecting the economy, but it is the so-called digital economy that has the potential to make a significant contribution to future prosperity in europe. in my view, the eu should also seek to develop the potential of the single market by facilitating online and cross-border trade between member states. in this context, attention should also be paid to the modernisation of vat legislation in order to promote the digital single market. one example is the vat rates for books, which illustrates the shortcomings of the current legislation. member states may apply reduced vat rates to the supply of books, but for e-books, for example, the basic vat rate is at least 15%. such a form of discrimination is hardly acceptable, given the growth potential of this market segment. i think it is appropriate to stress the need for the eu to be ambitious and to make the necessary efforts to eliminate the inconsistencies in the existing legal framework. helping businesses to develop and offer new pan-european online services should be a priority in the modernisation of vat legislation.

commissioner, governor, in 2010, the european central bank, despite the disagreement of several countries, applied the mechanism for buying bonds of euro area countries on secondary markets. but in the past few days, for the first time, she has failed to sterilize these purchases. it needed to withdraw eur 203,5 billion from the interbank market, but demand for its seven-day sterilisation operations was eur 194,2 billion. this tells us that european banks are holding cash and not providing it to the central bank, but also that the volume of bonds being purchased is becoming too large for the bank to be able to sterilize it and not increase the amount of euros in the financial system by buying bonds. if the trend of unsuccessful sterilisation operations were to continue, this would mean a kind of quantitative easing for the euro area and thus a negative impact on the purchasing power of the european currency. therefore, mr governor, the european central bank's policy needs to be modified very sensitively in order to better protect its currency and the price stability of the euro area.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 provides for the different forms of assistance that may be granted from structural fund contributions. member states introduced these forms of aid during the 2000-2006 programming period by setting up specific funds and by means of repayable assistance provided through other instruments. by contrast, council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 does not define aid as repayable or non-repayable aid. it contains provisions on financial engineering instruments, but these provisions are narrowly defined. this regulation does not seem to cover repayable aid. however, member states continued to use the repayable forms of aid on the basis of the positive experience of the previous programming period. it is therefore necessary to provide in regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 that the recovery aid may be co-financed by the structural funds. and i also think it's important to provide clarity on the legality of existing legal practice. it is necessary to ensure legal clarity and certainty in relation to the repayment assistance and financial engineering instruments. i believe that the monitoring of financial engineering instruments is appropriate, but that other reporting obligations by member states should be adjusted.

in writing. − the european central bank has so far been very successful in keeping hicp inflation at around 2%, despite several shocks at the macro-financial level and volatile commodity prices, and at a time of low average gdp growth in the union. however, the impact of higher interest rates on economic growth in the euro area is worrying, and this could make the already slow recovery in the euro area, especially in its weakest economies, more difficult. in accordance with article 282 tfeu, the primary objective of the ecb is to maintain price stability, which contributes to financial stability and adequate liquidity in financial markets. on the contrary, financial instability poses a serious risk to price stability over the medium term, as it impedes the smooth functioning of the monetary policy transmission mechanisms. the persisting or even worsening lack of economic convergence remains a structural problem for the single monetary policy in the euro area. the impact of monetary policy on the different euro area member states also varies considerably, and this asymmetry is expected to worsen if the ecb raises interest rates. in several member states, most loans are indexed to short-term interest rates. for this reason, too, there is an urgent need for common fiscal management at union level. i believe that much closer international coordination is needed to increase the stability of the global monetary system.
in writing. − reducing early school leaving appears to be essential to achieving many of the key objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. it promotes, in particular, the achievement of two of them: to achieve so-called smart growth by improving education and training levels, and so-called inclusive growth by removing one of the biggest risk factors of unemployment and poverty. the reasons for early school leaving vary considerably between countries and even within regions. i believe that policies to reduce early school leaving need to be adapted to the specific situation within a region or country, as it is not possible to reach a single solution that benefits all member states. this phenomenon is shown to occur more frequently in disadvantaged and vulnerable groups, such as young people with special educational needs. early school leaving subsequently results in social disadvantage and retains the risk of social exclusion. as early school leaving is a complex phenomenon that cannot be tackled by education and training alone, i believe it is essential to integrate measures to promote the reduction of early school leaving rates into all relevant policies for children and young people.
in writing. − poor performance is one of the main causes of school dropout. i agree that a common cause of failure in children is that school curricula are not adapted to the needs of children's age and socially determined interests. the uniform educational system makes it difficult to personalize the work to be done with the student. for pupils with special educational needs or behavioural difficulties, a personalised approach is in the best interests of the pupils. for these students, it is only possible to achieve a positive result in smaller classes. we know that teaching assistants are a great help for teachers and students, but they are present in very limited numbers (due to budget) in schools, and it would be justified to extend them to students with special needs, because they receive special help and attention. i support the proposal that every high school establish a counseling service so that schools not only have a teaching role but also provide emotional support for students. i support the second chance approach, which would allow the out-of-school youth to reintegrate.

in writing. − if you have since 2007, the european union has been rationalising its geographical cooperation with developing countries in asia, central asia and latin america and with iraq, iran, yemen and south africa under regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 december 2006 establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation. the eu has a strategic interest in strengthening the diverse links with these countries, particularly in the areas of economic, trade, academic and scientific exchanges, and therefore needs a financial instrument to finance such measures, which by their nature do not qualify for official development assistance. to this end, four preparatory actions were established under the budgetary procedures in 2007 and 2008: trade and scientific exchanges with india, trade and scientific exchanges with china, cooperation with middle-income countries in asia and cooperation with middle-income countries in latin america. the review of the regulation has identified inconsistencies in the provisions excluding costs relating to taxes, duties or other charges as unjustified. in the interests of consistency, it is necessary to bring those provisions into line with the other instruments and i therefore consider that it is desirable to amend regulation (ec) no 1934/2006 accordingly.
in writing. − the commission adopted a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1889/2006 establishing a financing instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights in the world on 21 april 2009. the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr) is one of the external financing instruments covered by the package. the eidhr and the development cooperation instrument are the only eu external financing instruments that do not provide for an exception to the principle that costs related to taxes, duties and other charges are not eligible for eu funding. in all other instruments in this field, financing of these costs is made possible on a case-by-case basis in order to ensure the proper implementation of programmes and projects. this flexibility is important because the inflexible formulation of the eidhr and dci instruments can make it very difficult to finance an action through external aid. the commission proposal aims to bring the relevant provision into line with other development aid instruments.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1172/98 of 25 may 1998 on statistical returns in respect of the carriage of goods by road has been substantially amended several times. in the light of further amendments, it is appropriate, for reasons of clarity, to recast this directive. in order to fulfil the tasks entrusted to the commission in the context of the common transport policy, it is justified that the commission should have at its disposal comparable, reliable, harmonised, regular and comprehensive statistical data on the volume and development of road freight transport by vehicles registered in the union and on the degree of utilisation of the vehicles providing such transport. it is necessary to compile comprehensive regional statistics with regard to the transport of goods and vehicle movements. at the same time, the scope of the powers delegated to the commission should not be too broad. for this reason, and in line with the similar approach adopted for the regulation on tourism statistics, i think it would be appropriate to adopt amendments aimed at limiting the scope of the powers delegated to the commission and laying down further conditions for the exercise of those powers.
in writing. − the european parliament and the council adopted in december 2006 a regulation laying down rules on short-term border traffic at the external land borders of the member states, allowing member states to exempt persons living in the border area from the general rules on border controls, including the visa requirement, the need to prove sufficient means of subsistence and the need to prove the purpose of the visit. the aim is to avoid creating obstacles to trade, social and cultural exchanges or regional cooperation with neighbours. when applying local border traffic, member states may conclude bilateral agreements with neighbouring countries aimed at addressing specific needs in relation to their respective neighbours. the links of the kaliningrad region with its neighbours have been significantly reduced, mainly as a result of the enlargement of the union in 2004. over the years, a number of eu initiatives have been developed to make it easier for kaliningrad residents to move around, but they have proved to be insufficient given the special geographical situation of kaliningrad. poland and the russian federation therefore request such an amendment of the regulation to take account of the specific situation of that region. the european commission is inclined to adopt a positive opinion if it is only a solution to a single situation. i also believe that it is desirable for poland to take the necessary measures to ensure easier movement and to avoid unnecessary complications that would impede that movement and introduce new obstacles.

the directive aims to facilitate and strengthen the protection of victims of crime, to prevent the commission of new offences and to mitigate the consequences of previous offences. we welcome the initiative to protect victims of violence and it is clearly necessary to bring it to a legal conclusion. safeguard measures taken in one member state must be recognised, administered and enforced. this system will enable the protected person to avoid parallel proceedings in different member states. there should also be appropriate mechanisms to prevent the same offence or another possibly more serious offence from being committed again. repeated offending is common in gender-based violence, although it also occurs in other forms of crime, such as trafficking in human beings or sexual abuse of minors. offenders are free to move around the european union. it is therefore necessary to allow the scope of protection measures taken in one member state to be extended in order to protect a victim of a crime who wishes to exercise the right of free movement. otherwise, victims of crime will face a difficult choice between renouncing the right of a union citizen to free movement and renouncing the right to protection. that is, of course, unacceptable.
providing protection to persons at risk of criminal offences when they move within the european union is a matter of different legal environments and traditions in the member states. therefore, the introduction of the european protection order also raises the need to carry out a comprehensive comparison of protection measures in civil matters in the various member states in order to achieve the same quality of protection of persons protected by a european union protection order. i am pleased that the european council, in accordance with the resolution on the roadmap for strengthening the protection of the rights of victims in criminal proceedings, supported the linking of the regulation on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters with the content of the european protection order directive. indeed, persons repeatedly threatened by criminals deserve a good, effective and comprehensive system of protection throughout the european union.

the european convention on human rights and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union also provide for fundamental rights of the defence. these include the right to be represented by a lawyer, the right to an interpreter and translation, the right to be informed of charges, the right to a periodic review of detention, and the right to be brought before a court. the current proposal aims to improve the rights of suspects or accused persons, in particular in the area of information on rights and charges. it also includes situations where a person is arrested on the basis of a european arrest warrant for the purpose of criminal prosecution or punishment. the existence of common minimum standards for those rights should facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition, thereby improving the functioning of judicial cooperation between the member states of the european union. i agree with the opinion of the committee on legal affairs that the plan to strengthen procedural rights has taken a piecemeal approach. the right to information is presented as the second measure of this plan, leading to a commission proposal which contains half of the bill of rights and partially excludes the other rights. these cover legal advice and legal aid, communication with relatives, employers and consular authorities, and the rights of suspects or accused persons belonging to the category of vulnerable persons. i think the right to information should be complemented by the other rights just mentioned. i thank you very much for your attention, commissioner, and i hope that you will take these suggestions into account in your report.
if a citizen in another eu country is faced with a criminal charge, he often has no idea what he will face in criminal proceedings. thus, a directive of the european parliament and of the council, which defines, in addition to the general right of a party to be informed of procedural rights, two specific types of rights. the right to be informed of the charges and the right of access to the file is a significant step towards ensuring that criminal proceedings against an accused person take place within the countries of the european union, at least in the basic outline, according to the related rules. compliance with common minimum standards on the right to information in criminal proceedings will also allow public authorities to avoid doubts that could later jeopardise the trustworthiness, fairness and legality of criminal proceedings. the proposed directive on the right to information in criminal proceedings will certainly contribute to a significant improvement in the rights of citizens of the european union in criminal proceedings.
last year, without an agreement with neighbouring countries, hungary unilaterally adopted a non-standard system of citizenship, which is allocated on ethnic grounds without any real connection between the citizen and the state. since hungary has refused and continues to postpone communication on this matter, the slovak republic has adopted the appropriate adjustment concerning citizenship. this includes the principle of the loss of citizenship of the slovak republic by voluntary acquisition of citizenship of another state. this principle is not contrary to european standards, but is contained in the european convention on citizenship and is also enshrined in the legislation of several member states of the european union. i therefore recommend to my hungarian colleagues in the european parliament that instead of hysterical nationalist outbursts, they put pressure on the government in budapest to start proper negotiations on this issue with neighbouring states.
the debt crisis is a crisis of confidence. investors in financial markets are afraid to lend more money to governments that have irresponsibly increased their spending. by not implementing reforms, they increased the public sector debt. as the economies of the eu member states are interconnected, the right balance needs to be struck between the responsibility of the states for the economy and solidarity when the economic and social order in one of the member states is threatened with disruption. but massive interventions by the european central bank must not become the standard measure that countries will use every time they get into trouble because of bad economic policies. the consequences would be catastrophic not only for europe but for the whole world. it is necessary to make use of the existing legal framework based on the treaty of lisbon. the convening of a new convention and a series of negotiations will require much more time than europe has at its disposal today.
i agree with the author of the report, mr sturdy, that the wide range of non-tariff measures used in international trade complicates relations between individual countries and economic groups. however, i am convinced that a correct and fair solution must be sought, especially at global level, because, as the author of the report rightly points out, many of these measures, such as technical standards or health certificates, are legitimate. however, measures that are clearly protectionist are also often used and we should eliminate them together. however, this is in the interest of all relevant economies and a common platform for exchanging views and finding solutions is therefore the best way forward.

everyone suspected or accused of committing a crime must be informed of his or her rights and these rights must be respected. only then can equality before the law and the administration of justice be guaranteed. this equality, as well as the right to a fair trial, is still guaranteed throughout the eu today. the series of directives to which this directive belongs sets out a minimum standard of information in criminal proceedings. they are intended to facilitate the exercise of those rights. this is necessary because today we have freedom of movement, freedom to settle and work in any country, and the way justice is administered differs from country to country. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of fundamental rights.
a europe without borders is already a given for us, and we don't think much about it. freedom to travel and settle in another member state, to find work and to start a family must also be guaranteed for victims of crime, for anyone at risk of violence. borders are no longer a barrier to criminals, so neither should the protection of victims. some may feel that the adoption of this directive is taking too long. two years of legislative procedures is not a short time. it will take another three years for member states to transpose this directive into their national law. this is to preserve one of the fundamental freedoms which, unlike financial and fiscal policy, is essential for the existence of a united europe. nevertheless, i find this method to be preferable, even though it takes longer to use. it respects the views, laws and values of the member states.
i'm all for simplifying the administration of applying legal immigrants to the job market. but we must not forget the principle of subsidiarity. i also want to remind you that legal migration is not the real solution to the demographic crisis in europe. the number of workers who will be laid off will increase every year. the ratio of pensioners to the number of workers will increase. i ask myself, how many legal immigrants will we need in 20 years if we fail to reverse this trend? legal immigration is just buying time. the only real solution to the demographic problem is family mainstreaming, a policy that takes into account the interests of the family at all times. until the commission and the governments of the member states understand this, we will never have enough legal migrants in europe.

several european union countries have taken measures to restrict the use of phosphates in detergents. phosphates are synthetic substances that are found in household detergents, washing machines and automatic washing machines, and after use, they end up in our water systems. there they cause excessive algal growth, which produces toxins and causes the death of fish and plants. however, measures by countries restricting the use of phosphates are ineffective, as both washing machine fillers and automatic washing machines are covered by mutual recognition regulations. a pragmatic way of tackling this problem is to adopt regulations on the permissible amount of phosphorus in detergents used in washing machines and automatic washing machines in standard filling units. adopting such harmonised rules would then help us to act in a uniform manner also in our communications with third countries. that would protect us as a whole, the european union.

in writing. the fruit juice market in the european union accounts for 10% of the total consumption of soft drinks. as regards the breakdown of this market, the production of fruit juices from concentrate is predominant compared to juices produced directly. as far as the world fruit juice market is concerned, the european union countries are largely supplied by the spanish market and by brazil. directive 2001/112/ec of 20 december 2001 relating to fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption lays down specific provisions concerning the production, composition and labelling of fruit juices and similar products in order to promote their free movement within the european union. i believe that these rules should be adapted to technical progress and take account of developments in relevant international standards. the ordinary legislative procedure provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union will apply to this newly proposed directive. this will now take account of the redefinition of the commission's powers (articles 290 and 291 of the treaty). consequently, the proposed directive amends articles 7 and 8 of the current directive by including all implementing measures in the category of delegated acts.
in writing. − phosphates from detergents have a negative impact on water management. they contribute to the accelerated growth of algae and higher plants, thus disturbing the ecological balance in our waters, especially in particularly vulnerable areas such as the baltic sea and the danube basin. in 2010, the commission put forward a proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 648/2004 on detergents by introducing restrictions on phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household detergents, and its proposal is very welcome. but there is another source of phosphates, and that is from automatic dishwasher detergents. the general objective of this proposal is, in particular, to reduce the negative impact of such substances on the aquatic environment. however, national legislation in the eu is already reflecting a trend away from the use of phosphates in detergents, with some member states seeking to apply restrictions to household detergents and some already imposing restrictions on these products used in automatic dishwashers. i welcome the establishment of a reasonable time limit for phosphorus in detergents, which can thus support the necessary innovation to accelerate the transition to phosphate-free formulations, but at the same time also allow sufficient time to reduce the negative consequences for manufacturers. this will also ensure harmonisation in the internal market.
in writing. − the kingdom of morocco is an african country with a population of approximately 32 million. morocco is currently a privileged partner of the european union and the largest recipient of eu funding under the european neighbourhood policy. the union is morocco's most important export market, its main public and private external investor and its most important tourism market. morocco has long been an important economic pillar, particularly the fishing industry, and the country is considered the largest fish market in africa, with the fishing sector estimated to provide some 400 000 jobs. the eu and the kingdom of morocco concluded a fisheries partnership agreement on 22 may 2006, which entered into force on 28 february 2007. following the expiry of the initial protocol, the european commission, acting on a mandate from the council, negotiated with the kingdom of morocco the extension of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement for one year. the council has not yet adopted the new protocol, but the european parliament must give its consent. i believe it is right that the european parliament has given its consent and at the same time instructed its president to forward this position to the council, the commission and the governments and parliaments of the member states and the kingdom of morocco.
in writing. − the european parliament, taking into account the proposal of the conference of presidents and also having regard to its decision of 15 july 2009 on the number of members of parliamentary committees, decided to amend the number of members of parliamentary standing committees. with the entry into force of protocol no 36 to the treaty of lisbon, new members are entitled to sit in the european parliament and its bodies, making full use of their rights. the changes in the number of members concerned twenty parliamentary committees and two subcommittees (the subcommittee on human rights and the subcommittee on security and defence). parliament also decided that committee chairs could have up to four vice-chairs. the decision to change the number of members of the standing committees was simultaneously forwarded by parliament, through its president, for information to the council and the commission.
in writing. − the european parliament, taking into account rule 198 of its rules of procedure and also its decision of 14 september 2009 on the number of interparliamentary delegations, delegations to joint parliamentary committees, delegations to parliamentary cooperation committees and to multilateral parliamentary assemblies, decided to amend the number of members in four interparliamentary delegations, namely the delegation for relations with the arabian peninsula, the delegation for relations with india, the delegation for relations with the korean peninsula and the delegation for relations with the republic of south africa. at the same time, with the entry into force of protocol 36 to the treaty of lisbon, new members are entitled to sit in the european parliament and its bodies and to exercise their rights to the full. the ep also forwarded, through its president, this decision relating to the change in the number of members of interparliamentary delegations, delegations to joint parliamentary committees and delegations to parliamentary cooperation committees and multilateral parliamentary assemblies for information to the council and the commission.

the efforts to create a single european transport area are ambitious, but currently run into problems of divergent transport regulations. in particular, the development of international rail transport is severely limited by national measures. therefore, a reasonable degree of harmonisation of the rules for the different modes of transport, allowing smooth transport activities across the entire territory of the union without undue local constraints, is a fundamental prerequisite for the creation of a universal european transport area. however, common european rules should not only harmonise the rules governing the operation of the various modes of transport, but also the technical characteristics of the means of transport. more than a quarter of emissions are produced by the transport sector. administrative pressure to reduce emissions in all modes of transport should therefore be a permanent and serious part of european transport policy.

despite the fact that there is a large body of community legislation on safety and health at work, the practical experience of workers in everyday life shows that the legislation adopted is often not sufficient. ensuring respect for one of the fundamental rights, the right to health, requires regular modernisation of legislation and its implementing measures in line with the latest medical knowledge on health risks. i consider the main current problem to be the lack of attention paid to chemical hazards, which have a highly negative impact on workers. comprehensive studies of such risks are still lacking, although the incidence of cancer and other chronic diseases is increasing rapidly. workers should be informed truthfully and appropriately about the risks associated with long-term exposure to carcinogens, which unfortunately cannot yet be replaced. at the same time, the identification of such substances must lead to their replacement without undue delay.
