first of all, i'd like to thank my colleagues for asking the question. european policy must be an innovation orientation capable of ensuring a long-term and sustainable energy supply for the whole of the european union. the russian gas crisis, the fukushima nuclear disaster and the depletion of our fossil fuels are all driving us to find answers to the energy question of the future as soon as possible. the intelligent energy europe programme developed by the commission certainly represented such a direction. its main objective is to provide clean, safe and sustainable energy for future generations. it promotes energy efficiency, the use of renewable energy sources and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. not only can we help our small and medium-sized enterprises with this programme, but we can also stimulate innovative solutions, create jobs and support education and research. however, the scheme was not specifically included in the next scheme. i would therefore ask the commission to do everything possible to ensure that this programme continues to operate. i think that despite the concerns about fukushima, nuclear energy can be considered as a smart energy. it has been demonstrated that nuclear energy is capable of producing unlimited, clean, safe and carbon-free energy. such a power source could be the fusion reactor as a result of the iter project. nuclear energy should therefore be given a stable place in the intelligent energy programme.
to achieve sustainable economic growth, the european union needs to be secure in its energy resources. the union is currently heavily dependent on their imports, mainly from africa and asia. europe does not have the oil or gas resources to afford not to look for alternative energy solutions, so it was natural to launch the smart energy programme, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources and modern sustainable energy solutions. however, the smart energy programme is only scheduled to run until the end of 2013, and therefore we need to ask ourselves today how we will continue with the initiatives on innovative energy and solutions beyond 2013. i, like my colleagues, expect the european commission to give us an answer to this question, which is very topical today, in the near future.
the annual report on competition in the european union assesses the state of play of european competition policy. despite the union's extensive and numerous measures to promote fair and equitable competition in trade, our citizens still signal to us certain reservations about the fair functioning of operators on the european market. in particular, in the area of food prices, price fixing opacity is a very sensitive and closely monitored issue. a more precise cost analysis of prices and margins in all areas of the food supply chain could certainly contribute to the objectification of price levels and to the improvement of consumer confidence. similarly, the steady increase in energy prices is seen and marked by a strong distrust of consumers and a belief that energy suppliers are abusing their dominant position. greater transparency in energy pricing and better supervision by regulatory authorities could help to restore consumer confidence in this area as well. the absence of real competition in the mobile roaming market is also a problem that is reflected in prices and concerns most of our citizens on a daily basis. it is therefore important to monitor the level of competition continuously and to react promptly to distortions that arise.
in writing. competition policy is the key instrument that will enable the european union to build a dynamic, efficient and innovative internal market and to compete successfully on the global stage. however, protectionism and non-enforcement of competition rules can deepen and prolong the crisis. cartels are the most serious threat to competition, consumer welfare and the proper functioning of markets. we can't accept them even in a time of economic crisis. the temporary regime applicable to state aid has been beneficial as an initial response to the crisis, but its application cannot be unduly prolonged. the provisional measures and exemptions should be lifted as soon as possible and as soon as the economic situation allows otherwise the situation may not be sustainable. it is necessary to introduce a new, permanent system of regulation of the application of state aid rules in order to address the shortcomings identified in the pre-crisis legal system, in particular as regards the financial sector, as well as to correct the distortions that have arisen during the financial and economic crisis.
in writing. competition policy is a policy conducive to a healthy, competitive business environment. therefore, state aid must also be allocated only in such a way that it does not distort competition, favouring existing companies over newly created ones. it also does not favour large companies over smes, foreign investors over domestic ones. the granting of state aid must be subject to clear criteria, which must also be rigorously controlled. i support the request for a study of the application of state aid rules to determine whether the differences between member states do not cause distortions of competition. if a derogation is granted, it must be justified and in accordance with the rules that it does not unduly distort competition.
in writing. − in its resolution of 16 december 2010 on a new strategy for afghanistan, parliament identified a number of important issues concerning budgetary control of eu financial assistance to afghanistan. this country is among those receiving the majority of civil aid from the general budget of the union. however, it is of serious concern that a significant part of international aid is lost in the distribution chain, in particular through waste, excessive costs of intermediation and security, excessive invoicing and corruption. for this reason, it is essential that the commission oversees and monitors the costs and effectiveness of all eu assistance in afghanistan in order to improve its effectiveness. the overall objective of eu development assistance to afghanistan should be to support the long-term and sustainable development of the country, including the improvement of socio-economic standards, facilitating job creation and the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises, strengthening the education sector and ensuring gender equality. such assistance should further facilitate capacity building in the public administration, strengthen the rule of law and curb corruption, thereby helping to shift responsibility for security to the government of the islamic republic of afghanistan. i believe that there is an urgent need to increase aid effectiveness, as many development indicators still show no significant improvement and corruption and the long distribution chain of international aid remain the main obstacles to the provision of basic services to the population.
in writing. − afghanistan is a country that has been, and still is, torn by war and conflict. these conflicts continue to take a heavy toll on afghanistan and its people. afghanistan's territorial wars have characterized the country for virtually the entire 20th century. the terrorist attacks of 2001 and the presence of terrorist organisations in afghanistan have unfortunately not changed much. i therefore fully agree with my colleague geir who proposes direct aid to afghanistan from the european union budget, which is currently missing. i firmly believe that with strict financial control of such funding and expertise - whether from the eu or our american partners - we will be able to come up with a solution that will really help afghanistan. the most important areas, apart from the independence of the judiciary which was highlighted by mr geier, i consider to be improving the situation in the field of education. because only in this way can sustainable development be achieved and the situation be resolved in the long term.
in writing. − competition policy rules and practices are undergoing a constant process of adaptation in order to contribute to the eu's main objectives, which include building the single market, making it work for the benefit of consumers, and achieving a competitive social market economy. it is noteworthy that while the environment in which eu competition policy operates is undergoing profound changes such as rapid technological development, enlargement or globalisation, the various provisions of the 1957 treaty prohibiting certain anti-competitive agreements and the abuse of a dominant position are not affected by time, nor are the state aid provisions, which testifies to their inherent applicability in different circumstances. given the commission's exclusive competence in competition policy, as confirmed by the treaty of lisbon, the commission is empowered to adopt more detailed rules on how it intends to use its main instruments the provisions of the treaty relating to antitrust policy, the provisions on mergers and state aid. since the beginning of the implementation of eu competition policy, it has been characterised by two main priority features, namely its contribution to the construction and maintenance of the internal market and its contribution to the interests of consumers. at the same time, competition policy supports the european union's main objectives, as enshrined in the treaties: a competitive market, economic, social and territorial cohesion and sustainable development.
in writing. − the commission's 2010 competition report is essentially about limiting and remedying the economic crisis processes and their consequences that have recently started. for four decades, competition policy has been the essential foundation of economic cooperation since the beginning of the community. today, market movements distorted by the crisis must also be addressed by proper regulation. the commission has tried to respond effectively to the economic crisis by adopting state aid rules within the framework of competition policy. i agree with the rapporteurs that a global approach to competition rules is also needed. the report covers a number of sectors, including the call for the swift implementation of the internal energy market package to achieve an open and competitive single energy market. the introduction of effective cost analysis at all stages of the food supply chain is equally important to protect consumers' interests. the commission's guidelines on the rescue and restructuring of the banking sector are also inevitable and their consideration and application will have to be monitored. i agree that future temporary state aid to the banking sector should be subject to stricter conditions and that more ethical retail lending should also be given due consideration. the market distortions caused by the crisis can only be remedied by a common union decision. i voted in favour of the report of the economic and monetary committee, as i believe that competition policy is a key factor in developing the eu into a dynamic, well-functioning and innovative internal market and in strengthening competitiveness on the world market.
in writing. − the financial and economic crisis that erupted in autumn 2008 continues and member states are at risk of a long-term recession. i agree that protectionism and non-enforcement of competition rules will in no way contribute to solving the crisis. on the contrary, a well-designed competition policy should help to build a dynamic and innovative internal market that can compete successfully in the world. cartels remain the most serious threat to competition, consumer welfare and the proper functioning of markets, even in times of crisis, and the imposition of fines as an enforcement tool is therefore justified. however, i believe that the commission should examine individual cases with particular care and ensure that the amount of the fines does not irreparably jeopardise the economic viability of the undertaking concerned, leading to its bankruptcy, liquidation and consequently also a high level of job losses. the crisis requires that responses to the challenges posed take account of the complex economic and social context and do not penalise even more eu citizens.
in writing. − point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management allows the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) via the flexibility instrument with an annual ceiling of eur 500 million over and above the relevant headings of the financial framework. the rules applicable to the financial contributions from the egf are laid down in regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund. on 9 october 2009, france submitted an application egf/2009/019 fr/renault for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in renault s.a.s. and its seven subsidiaries in france. the request refers to 1 384 redundancies at renault s.a.s. and its six suppliers and to a further 3 061 redundancies at renault s.a.s. and its seven suppliers outside the reference period, but which are covered by the same voluntary redundancy scheme. after a thorough examination of the application, the commission concluded that the conditions for granting a financial contribution were met.
in writing. − article 255 of the treaty establishing the european union, as amended by the treaty of amsterdam, confers on citizens of the european union and on natural and legal persons residing or having their registered office in a member state the right of access to european parliament, council and commission documents. the principles and limits governing this right of access were laid down in regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 regarding public access to european parliament, council and commission documents, which entered into force on 3 december 2001. however, since it has been substantially amended several times, it is appropriate, in the interests of clarity and better understanding, to recast that regulation. transparency in the legislative process is of paramount importance to citizens. the institutions should therefore actively disseminate documents that are part of the legislative process. and such actions should be encouraged in other areas as well. however, given the very sensitive nature of certain documents, it is necessary and essential to bear in mind that they must be handled in a special and responsible manner in all circumstances.
in writing. − following the erika oil tanker accident and the significant oil pollution caused by it, the commission proposed a regulation at the end of 2000 establishing the european maritime safety agency (emsa) as a body of expertise to guarantee a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and prevention of pollution from ships in the eu. regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 was adopted by the european parliament and the council on 27 june 2002. the regulation entered into force in august of the same year and emsa started its activities in march 2003. in accordance with article 22 of that regulation, the management board provided in 2007 for an independent external evaluation of the implementation of that regulation. on the basis of this evaluation, it issued recommendations in june 2008 for changes to the regulation as well as to the agency and its working procedures. some provisions need to be clarified and updated, and emsa should also be given a range of additional tasks reflecting the evolution of maritime safety policy at eu and international level. oil and gas exploration and production activities at sea pose risks to maritime transport and the marine environment. for this reason too, it is important that the agency, within its capabilities, makes the necessary efforts related to the endeavour to minimise such risks.

in writing. − the main objective of the newly created surveillance mechanism is to prevent and correct macroeconomic imbalances in the european union. under regulation (eu) no 1176/2011, the other objectives of the new mechanism include the sustained convergence of the economic performance of the member states and closer coordination of economic policies. in the current economic situation, it is essential that the macroeconomic surveillance framework is established and operational as soon as possible. member state governments must be prepared to act on any problems that may arise, as this is the only way to ensure that the supervisory framework has the desired effect. in the context of the compilation of future macroeconomic tables (which may contain a wide range of indicators), these indicators must be based on independent and verifiable official statistical data from the european statistical system and the european system of central banks. i believe that the transparent implementation of this new policy instrument is of great importance and that it is therefore necessary for the commission to ensure that all documents or working papers relating to the scoreboard are delivered to parliament and the council on an equivalent basis.
in writing. − transport is a key element for the european economy and society. it is crucial for the internal market, for the living standards of citizens, enabling them to travel freely, and also contributes to economic growth and job creation. however, it must be sustainable in the light of the new challenges facing society. however, given its global nature, the effectiveness of individual actions requires strong international cooperation. the future prosperity of the european continent will depend on the ability of all its regions to maintain full and competitive integration into the world economy. and efficient transport plays a very important role in achieving this goal. obstacles to the smooth functioning of effective competition in the internal market remain. the objective of the next decades should therefore be to create a genuine single european transport area by removing all remaining barriers between the different modes of transport and national systems. i believe that the appropriate way to achieve this objective is also to simplify the integration process and to encourage the emergence of multinational and multimodal operators.
in writing. − the european union has set itself the task of building an area of freedom, security and justice and, in accordance with article 6 of the treaty on european union, it respects human rights and fundamental freedoms and thus assumes the obligations it must fulfil in order to fulfil this commitment. the conditions of detention and the management of detention facilities are primarily the responsibility of the member states. deficiencies such as prison overcrowding and alleged ill-treatment of detainees can undermine the trust that must underpin judicial cooperation in criminal matters, based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and other judicial decisions of eu member states. respect for fundamental rights standards and the necessary convergence of the rights of suspects and accused persons and procedural rights in criminal proceedings are key to ensuring mutual trust between member states in the area of freedom, security and justice. conditions of detention are of particular importance for the application of the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions in the area of freedom, security and justice. at the same time, however, i consider it equally important that member states allocate adequate resources to restructuring and modernising prison facilities, to protecting the rights of detainees, or to their successful rehabilitation and preparation for release and reintegration into society.
in writing. − partnership and cooperation agreements were concluded with the countries of the former soviet union in the late 1990s. as the eu had a bilateral agreement with uzbekistan, it decided to include article 16 in the partnership and cooperation agreement, thus clearly excluding textiles from that agreement. as regards the other sectors, the partnership and cooperation agreement provided for a mutual provision of a 'most favoured nation' clause. from an economic point of view, however, this agreement should not be overestimated. uzbekistan is the world's fifth largest producer of cotton and is the world's third largest exporter of cotton. the political and economic system in uzbekistan is controlled by the state. although cotton is produced on private farms, the harvest must be handed over to state-owned companies at a price set by the state. in addition, during the cotton harvest, government employees mobilize children as a cheap source of labor, sending them to cotton plantations, and schools are closed during the harvest. many international organizations have expressed concern over the use of forced child labor in uzbekistan over the years. i believe it is essential to insist that the government of uzbekistan fully implement the official prohibition of this practice in uzbek legislation and international conventions. reforms are needed to modernise and motorise the agricultural sector, which would help to eliminate forced child labour.
in writing. - my colleagues. the ec-uzbekistan partnership and cooperation agreement has been the cornerstone of bilateral relations since its entry into force in 1999. the main issue on the table at present is the deepening of cooperation, particularly in the context of textile trade. uzbekistan is the third largest exporter of cotton in the world. it is in the cotton harvest that we encounter our greatest obstacle. the issue of forced child labour in cotton harvesting is a topic that is still unresolved. uzbekistan has made significant progress in combating this problem in recent years, and these changes and reforms have been noted and appreciated by unicef observers, but it is still not enough. one of the last things uzbekistan needs to do is allow monitoring by observers from the international labour organization, ilo. i have personally visited uzbekistan several times and i have seen that the country is willing to cooperate in this area as well and is interested in the complete elimination of forced child labour. i therefore call on our uzbek partners to allow access for ilo staff so that we can finally move forward. i firmly believe that together we can find a way to reach an agreement.
in writing. − the right to live and work in another eu country is one of the eu's fundamental freedoms, guaranteeing equal treatment and protection against discrimination on grounds of nationality, an essential element of citizenship of the union recognised in the treaties. however, two member states face obstacles to the right to work in the territory of another member state. the free movement of workers thus represents a positive socioeconomic example for the eu and its member states, a milestone in the process of eu integration, economic development and a counterweight to the negative effects of the economic crisis, contributing to the creation of a stronger economic power ready to face the challenges of global change. member states which have not applied transitional measures in relation to the free movement of workers from member states which acceded to the eu in 2004 and 2007 do not have any negative consequences. however, many member states have chosen to continue to apply restrictions on their labour markets (as regards nationals of romania and bulgaria) which result from political pressures rather than from justified negative effects on the economy and the labour market. i believe that the restrictive transitional periods should be abolished so that bulgarian and romanian citizens can enjoy the right to equal treatment enshrined in the treaties, thus ensuring fair competition between businesses and avoiding social and economic dumping.
in writing. − central asia is of strategic importance to europe, a well-known but often underestimated one. in implementing the strategy, the eu launched important initiatives and programmes over the past four years to support priorities such as good governance, the rule of law, human rights and democratisation, education and training, economic development, trade and investment, transport and energy, environmental sustainability and water management, and tackling common threats and challenges. since 2007, however, the world has undergone significant changes. important (but tragic) events have taken place in central asia, and new political influences have emerged in the region. all this is prompting the european institutions to rethink their policy towards central asia, to assess what has already been achieved and to propose new approaches to adapt their activities to a region facing many threats that may also have an impact on europe. in this context, the eu should revise its approach to central asia in an appropriate manner, as it has done with its nearest neighbour. for it cannot care about ethics in one part of the world and not react to violations of its values in another part of the world. this is how her credibility is compromised. however, human rights and the rule of law must be promoted above all in all european activities and initiatives.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i consider the relations between the european union and central asia to be of paramount importance. the countries belonging to this region have had a really turbulent history, during the cold war they were part of the soviet union and after gaining independence they have been and are still undergoing a difficult test of the sustainability of democracy. strong authoritarian regimes, such as the government of president niyazov in turkmenistan, or the recent violent unrest in kyrgyzstan that led to a coup d'état, are just some examples of the complicated situation in central asia. mrs kiil-nielsen says in her report that we need to approach talks and negotiations with the countries of central asia with the same emphasis and rigor as we approach our immediate neighbours. now, i don't want to suggest that we should be more lenient on human rights in the case of central asians or that we should forgive them something that we wouldn't forgive other partners. however, i would point out that in approaching these countries we should take into account the different culture, the political behaviour of their citizens and the different stages of democratic transition.
in writing. − health and safety at work is currently one of the most important and developed aspects of eu employment and social affairs policy. the adoption and practical application of a wide range of union legislation over the last decades has made it possible to improve working conditions in the eu member states and to make great progress in reducing work-related accidents and diseases. health and safety at work, for economic as well as for human reasons, deserve a great deal of attention in the eu's political agenda, as they play an important role in enhancing the competitiveness and productivity of enterprises and in contributing to the viability of social security systems. they result in reduced costs for accidents, injuries and illnesses and in greater motivation of workers. the burden of occupational accidents and diseases on public and private social security systems is enormous and requires an integrated, coordinated and strategic approach as well as cooperation between the main stakeholders in the eu. i believe that it is desirable in the future to focus on the promotion and use of risk reduction technologies that constitute dangerous substances in the event of occupational accidents in the framework of future legislation on safety and health. it would also be appropriate to consider that these technologies replace the use of chemical and radioactive substances where appropriate.
in writing. − to protect the rights of our workers and to address their current problems, the eu strategy on safety and health at work must keep pace with the technological and demographic changes of recent years. the reduction of the rate of accidents and diseases at work should be one of the key objectives of the strategy. i consider the protection of workers in high-risk categories to be particularly important. this includes workers in hazardous sectors such as construction and chemical workers, as well as people with disabilities, young workers and women. stress at work and the psychological pressure of deadlines are also very significant negative factors today. this is primarily due to poor work organisation and management style. i fully agree with the view that we must ensure that the austerity measures brought about by the economic crisis do not in any way compromise safety at work. it is important that the standards are uniform across the member states. unfortunately, this has not been the case in recent years, but i am confident that harmonization in this area will be successful.
azerbaijan is a friendly country of the european union and is making efforts to progressively democratise its political environment. however, islamic influence is quite intense in neighboring azerbaijan due to the radical iranian regime. the murder of rafik tagi, probably carried out on the basis of a fatwa by an iranian cleric, is evidence of this. the european union must be more active in its efforts to win over the azerbaijani people to a civilized democratic way of life. therefore, it is appropriate to express some concern to the azerbaijani government over the superficial conduct of the investigation into the murder of rafik tagi. we must work to ensure that the regime in azerbaijan actually cooperates with the european union in building a democratic system.
for the efd group. the status of women in islamic countries is complicated by persistent religious customs and traditions. especially in the more remote regions and areas controlled by radical religious political groups, brutal medieval customs continue to be used. the european union's efforts to change the mindset of the people of these countries towards a more humane and cultured coexistence are therefore of paramount importance. the union's activities in support of shelters for women who need to protect themselves from domestic violence or humiliation in the family, but also in public, are of paramount importance. but in addition to providing real humanitarian assistance to women and girls on the ground, we must also put continuous pressure on state authorities to use all their influence in society to suppress these brutal practices against women and girls. the state authorities must be the bearers of civilized and humane coexistence of society and decisively fight against the monstrosity of the customs of the past.
in writing. the eu's cooperation agreement with pakistan states in article 1 that: 'respect for human rights and democratic principles, as set out in the universal declaration of human rights (...), constitutes an essential element of this agreement.' i therefore supported the joint resolution tabled in which parliament asks the commission and, in particular, european diplomacy to submit a detailed report on how pakistan is complying with its commitment. it is clear that human rights violations, especially of women and christians, are commonplace in pakistan. however, it is not entirely clear what the commission, which is equally bound by the existing agreement, is doing and could do. diplomacy knows the mechanisms that can be used in such cases. it is up to us to prove that human rights are important to europeans not only on paper but also in real life.
for the efd group. the tunisian people, as one of the leaders of the arab spring, were able to overthrow the bin ali regime and fight for their right to a better life. but the people in the police or the judiciary, who are doing their jobs as they were taught under the previous regime, have not changed with the regime's departure. the incident at tunis-carthage airport, where zakaria boughira was detained, is clear evidence of this. building a new, hopefully decent and better society in tunisia will surely take some time. the new administration will have to rebuild and re-train its law enforcement and judicial bodies so that they are no longer seen by the tunisian population as repressive elements brutally suppressing freedom, but as state elements protecting their peaceful life. in addition to the justified criticism of such failures, as demonstrated by the tunisian police in november in their crackdown on moroccan fans, we could also help the new state by helping train police officers to prevent such crackdowns in the future.
